strategy_name: Symmetrical triangle / volatility-compression expansion
mechanism: prices oscillating in a tightening range compress volatility; resolution is a large expansion, and a failed breakout on one side accelerates the move against the trapped side
setup_summary: Daily: several weeks of tightening highs/lows form a symmetrical triangle (volatility contraction). The book's variant: price first rallies above the upper channel (drawing in bulls) and fails, then short the break of the lower channel below the 20/50-day MAs; the long mirror applies on the upper-channel break.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: break below the lower channel (or above the upper channel for longs). Invalidation: close back inside the triangle.
risk_geometry: Entry: short ~30-40c below the failed-breakout low / below MAs. Stop: above the failed-breakout high. Target: prior swing low. Expiry: short, days.
quote: It is merely a pattern that predicts a large expansion of volatility
chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'Break of a Symmetrical Triangle Chart Pattern' (FXI)
notes: Direction-neutral compression-to-expansion mechanism; book trades the failed-breakout variant. Compression is measurable as a declining ATR/range ratio in the window.
book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

strategy_name: Intraday relative-strength momentum (top-down)
mechanism: instruments showing the largest gap-adjusted strength from the open while trading in the top third of their intraday range tend to lead the session; buying the strongest into strength captures continuation
setup_summary: Intraday: rank sector indexes by % change at open+5min and open+30min; keep the one with the largest move since the open (gap-adjusted), still in the top (bottom) third of its intraday range, with first-30min volume >= its 5-day average; buy the strongest ETF within the sector on a 0.382 Fibonacci retracement of the first-30-min range or on a break above the first-30-min high.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 0.382 retracement fills or opening-range breakout; if no retracement by open+45min, 'correction by time' -> enter at market. Invalidation: index falls out of the top/bottom third of its intraday range.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit at 0.382 retracement or market on breakout/time-correction. Stop: below intraday swing or the preplanned multiweek stop. Target: day-trade via 5/15-min MAs and trendlines, or the multiweek target.
quote: sectors that don't fall with the broad market will be the first ones to rally to new highs when the major indexes eventually bounce
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'Identifying Relative Strength Intraday'
notes: The 9:35/10:00 session anchors do not exist in a 24/7 market, but the cross-sectional relative-strength core ('buy the leaders, not the laggards') is testable with trailing-window strength across perp instruments.
book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

strategy_name: Minimum 2:1 reward/risk gate with extension filter
mechanism: only take trades whose structural target is at least twice the stop distance, and skip entries too far extended from their breakout pivot where downside risk outweighs upside
setup_summary: Before entry require (target - entry) / (entry - stop) >= 2. Do not buy after a large quick extension (e.g. >20% in three days) or at an extended 52-week high; prefer the breakout-then-tight-consolidation base over the extended move.
trigger_invalidation: Skip the trade if R:R < 2:1 or entry is beyond the breakout pivot by more than a few percent.
risk_geometry: Risk = points entry-to-stop; reward = points entry-to-projected target.
quote: If the downside risk outweighs the profit potential, don't make the trade... especially if the reward is at least double the risk (2:1 reward/risk ratio)
chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Always Use Reward/Risk Ratios'
notes: The extension filter is especially relevant on leveraged perps where late entries into extended moves face deep pullbacks.
book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

strategy_name: Stop wiggle room below obvious levels (withstanding stop hunts)
mechanism: stops clustered at the obvious trendline/MA level are run first; a volatility-scaled buffer below obvious support avoids false stop-outs while keeping risk bounded
setup_summary: For 1-3 week holds, draw the 60/120-min uptrend/downtrend line and place the stop below it by a volatility-scaled buffer (~0.2x ATR; 10c on a 50c ATR) rather than at it; never place a break-even stop exactly on an obvious trendline (OIH's breakeven coincided with the hourly uptrend line and was probed).
trigger_invalidation: Placement rule; thesis-invalidation remains a clean close beyond the buffer level.
risk_geometry: Stop ~1 point below the 20-day EMA or ~0.2x ATR below trendline support; looser stop paired with smaller share size.
quote: Is my stop placement too obvious? If it is, you can be assured that you will be stopped out, only to watch the stock or ETF reverse in the right direction
chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Withstanding Stop Hunts'
notes: Crypto has no specialist/market-maker, but liquidation clusters and MEV bots target obvious stop levels; the buffer principle transfers while the manipulator narrative is venue-specific.
book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

strategy_name: Sitting-on-hands (SOH) no-trade regime filter
mechanism: in regimes where breakouts fail, breadth diverges, volume dries up, or big news looms, edge is absent and standing aside preserves capital
setup_summary: Stand aside when: (a) major indexes diverge (one breaking down, another at new highs), (b) an elevated share of breakouts fail within a day or two, (c) aggregate volume runs well below its 50-day average, or (d) highly anticipated macro news is pending.
trigger_invalidation: Activate on any listed condition; deactivate when conditions normalize.
risk_geometry: No entry; cash is a valid position.
quote: The most consistently profitable professional traders are actually out of the markets more than they are in the markets
chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Know When to Be in SOH Mode'
notes: Measurable crypto analogs: BTC/ETH divergence, failing breakout breadth, declining perp volume, FOMC/CPI event windows.
book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

strategy_name: Breakout trigger discipline: confirm with an ATR-scaled buffer
mechanism: false breakouts are common at obvious levels; requiring price to exceed resistance by a volatility-scaled buffer makes the breakout self-confirming and filters fakeouts
setup_summary: The entry trigger is always above resistance / below support by a buffer (~0.2x ATR: QQQQ 3-day high 47.87 + 10c on a 50c ATR -> trigger 47.97-48.02) and is never pre-empted; if the trigger is not hit, there is no trade.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger must be touched/cleared; missing it means no entry (QQQQ probed only 5c above the 3-day high before reversing).
risk_geometry: Entry: break of level + ATR buffer; stop below/above the level; target: structure. Paying a slightly worse price for a higher confirmation probability.
quote: It's always better to pay a slightly higher price for entry, in exchange for a better chance of not getting sucked into a false breakout
chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Proper Trigger Prices' + QQQQ example
notes: Refines the backlog breakout_retest family; wick-throughs above resistance are frequent on 24/7 crypto, so the buffer is a practical fakeout filter.
book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

strategy_name: Target-and-exit at structural level (take the gift)
mechanism: covering at the predetermined structural target (test of prior support/resistance) captures the bulk of the move with minimal risk even when continuation is possible; greed invites giving it back
setup_summary: Set the target at a prior swing low/high and cover on the test of that level regardless of whether further move is likely (IWM target = January low; FXI target = Jan 10 low; OIH covered on the test of its prior low). If the exit looks premature, the resulting bounce offers a better reentry.
trigger_invalidation: Exit at the predetermined structural target; a reversal before target is handled by the protective stop.
risk_geometry: Target = structural prior extreme; exit on the test; reentry on the subsequent bounce.
quote: I covered on the test of the prior low, the original downside price target having been satisfactorily achieved
chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 IWM short (also FXI, OIH)
notes: Supports structural (S/R-based) targets over pure fixed-R targets in V8 risk_geometry.
book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

strategy_name: Consolidation-to-expansion volatility breakout (long straddle/strangle thesis)
mechanism: tight consolidation precedes a large-magnitude move in either direction; profit comes from the expansion exceeding the premium paid, not from direction
setup_summary: After a period of consolidation bounded by support/resistance, forecast a large-magnitude move away from the consolidation (the book's setup for long straddles/strangles). The magnitude must exceed the premium: breakevens are strike +/- debit. In perp terms: tight range compression followed by directional expansion; direction at entry is not required, only magnitude.
trigger_invalidation: Entry after consolidation; thesis fails if no breakout occurs before the time stop (each day of no movement bleeds theta - 'death of a thousand cuts') or if the structure value breaches a preset price stop; breakevens at strike +/- premium define the magnitude the move must exceed.
risk_geometry: Entry after consolidation at the strike; stops = BOTH a price stop on the structure and a time stop (a date beyond which the position is not carried); target = breakeven distance (strike +/- premium).
quote: In this scenario, the trader of a long straddle or strangle should be looking for a large magnitude move (that is, a breakout) away from the strike price.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, 'Straddles and Strangles', 'Strategy Component Selection' (p. 119)
notes: The straddle/strangle structure is not perp-executable, but the market-timing thesis (consolidation -> expansion) is the core of tight-range breakout trading and can feed the existing breakout_retest backlog family (range-compression entry, trend-expansion exit). Time-stop discipline is mandatory since perp funding/carry plays the theta role.
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: Profit-banking roll while maintaining directional exposure
mechanism: as a winning directional trade progresses, periodically bank profit and reduce risk while keeping exposure in the direction of the move, then close fully when the move is judged over
setup_summary: Lifecycle rule for the successful position: when the underlying moves in the forecast direction, manage the winner by periodically taking money off the table while maintaining exposure (in options, rolling the long leg via vertical spreads; in perps, scaling out / trailing). Rolling 'maintains the exposure in the direction of the breakout, reduces risk and takes money off the table, and puts the trader in a strong psychological position'. Close entirely as soon as the move appears over; never leave residual short/opposing legs open.
trigger_invalidation: Continue rolling/scaling while the directional move persists; close fully when the trader feels the move is over or momentum fades; the short/opposite leg must be closed once the breakout is confirmed even if far OTM ('never... leave short option positions open, no matter how far out-of-the-money').
risk_geometry: Roll/scaling points at momentum pauses; profit banked at each roll; final close when the move ends; keep stops on any remaining opposite leg. Extra execution costs from each adjustment reduce profit.
quote: Rolling a long option position is an excellent way to manage a position that is 'going your way.' ... It maintains the exposure in the direction of the breakout. It reduces risk and takes 'money off the table.'
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Collars and Reverse-Collars', 'Managing the Successful Position' (p. 86)
notes: Directly applicable to trend-trade lifecycle: V8's position_scaling/break_even_stop vocabulary matches. The 'exit when the move is over' rule requires a momentum-based close signal (response feature group).
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: Trigger-price (pivot) anchored breakout
mechanism: a specific price level - the top/bottom of a consolidation - acts as the launch pad; the move only begins when price trades through the trigger
setup_summary: Identify the trigger/pivot price - the level whose trade-through is expected to launch a large move (e.g., the top of a range, or a consolidation boundary). Anchor the long exposure at the trigger to capture most of the forecast move, and place the opposite-side short at significant resistance (collar) or support (reverse-collar). Choose an expiry that comfortably covers the forecast time horizon with margin (book example: consolidation historically lasted 10-15 days, so choose the 60-day expiry over the 28-day).
trigger_invalidation: The trade is contingent on price trading through the trigger price; if the trigger is not reached by expiry the position 'fails to trigger' and must be rolled to the next cycle or closed. Stop-loss on the opposite short leg at the key support/resistance level, below which the forecast is wrong.
risk_geometry: Entry anchored at the trigger price; short-leg stop at significant resistance (collar) or support (reverse-collar); expiry = forecast time horizon plus buffer; cost kept near zero by choosing equidistant strikes.
quote: ABC is trapped in a range between 100.00 and 105.00. The trader believes that the next time it trades through 105.00 ABC is going to break out for a large upside move. In this case 105.00 is the trigger price. (In technical analysis lingo, this is sometimes referred to as the pivot price.)
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Collars and Reverse-Collars', 'What Is the Trigger Price of the Forecast Move?' (p. 82)
notes: The trigger/pivot anchoring is the structural core of breakout trading and feeds the existing breakout_retest / failed_breakout location logic. The expiry-with-margin rule transfers as a time-horizon buffer. The collar structure itself is not perp-executable.
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: Turtle Donchian Channel Breakout (S1 20-day / S2 55-day)
mechanism: A market making a new N-day high/low has sufficient momentum that the trend tends to persist; follow it and exit when the opposite channel breaks.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, enter LONG when close makes a new 20-bar (System One) or 55-bar (System Two) high; enter SHORT on a new 20/55-bar low. Exit on the opposite-direction 10-bar (S1) or 20-bar (S2) breakout, or on the 2N stop, whichever triggers first. No target, no retracement waiting — buy the breakout at market.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close makes new 20/55-bar channel extreme. Invalidated when price makes an opposite-direction 10/20-bar breakout (exit) or touches the 2N stop.
risk_geometry: Entry next bar open (book: 'entry on the next trading day'); stop = 2N (2×20-day ATR); no R-multiple target, exit is structure-based (opposite channel breakout) or 2N stop; no fixed expiry — position held while trend persists.
quote: System Two was the Turtles' longer-term trading system. It used an eleven-week breakout (fifty-five days) for an entry signal and a four-week breakout (twenty days) in the opposite direction for an exit.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'The Rules' (pp. 72-73)
notes: Canonical trend-following family, distinct from existing V8 trend_pullback (EMA-cross entry) and failed_breakout (liquidity_vacuum). 24/7 perp tape has no exchange gaps so channel highs/lows are well-defined; funding cost is the main drag on an always-in-market breakout system. Candidate to formalize after the active 3 experts are screened; shares the 'trend_continuation' mechanism family with trend_pullback.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Volatility-Scaled Unit Sizing (2% risk per unit)
mechanism: Equalizing each unit's dollar risk to a fixed fraction of equity (2%) makes every market/position comparable and keeps drawdown survivable while waiting for the rare large trend.
setup_summary: Size each unit so risk = 2% of current equity; contracts = (2% × equity) / (2N × contract value), rounded down to whole contracts. A 'unit' is the same risk in every market (one corn unit = one gold unit = one BTC unit).
trigger_invalidation: Unit size recomputed daily from current equity and current N (volatility). No invalidation — continuous position-sizing rule.
risk_geometry: Sizing rule only: fraction-of-equity risk (2%), volatility-normalized via 2N dollar risk, round down; cap 4-5 units per market.
quote: They bet a fixed 2 percent of their capital on hand on each trade. If they had $100,000, they would bet (or risk) 2 percent ($2,000) on each trade. Each 2 percent bet of their equity was called a 'unit.'
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'The Rules', Risk Management (pp. 83-86)
notes: Core position-sizing risk rule for V8's RiskGate. On leveraged perps this is the mechanism that prevents liquidation-driven ruin: risk per unit is defined as fraction-of-equity, not contract count. Rounding down and daily N update are directly mechanizable.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Turtle Pyramiding (add units at 1N intervals, stop ratchet)
mechanism: Reinforcing winners compounds the payoff of the rare big trend; ratcheting stops to the newest unit's 2N protects accumulated open profit without exiting early.
setup_summary: After a breakout entry, add one unit at each favorable 1N move (entry+1N, +2N, ...) up to a maximum of 5 units. Stops: 1/2N on the first trading day, then 2N thereafter; each time a unit is added, all stops are brought up to that newest unit's 2N stop (break-even ratchet).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger to add: price moves 1N in trade direction. All stops ride the newest unit's 2N; if the ratcheted stop is hit the whole position exits.
risk_geometry: Adds at +1N intervals, max 5 units; stop = 1/2N day one, then 2N behind the newest add; no R-multiple target — exit by stop or opposite-channel breakout; total risk to original equity is bounded by 2% per unit added.
quote: A new unit will be added at 105, 110, etc. Turtles could pyramid a maximum of 5 units. They set their stops at ½N on the first day of trading and from that point forward, 2N stops were used. Then, once the second unit was bought, both stops were brought up to the new unit's 2N stop.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'The Rules', Pyramiding (pp. 87-91)
notes: Position-scaling lifecycle behavior for V8's ExposureBook. Currently V8 holds ONE exposure per (instrument,direction); pyramiding is a scaling variant to test later against the single-unit baseline. On perps the 2N stop must account for liquidation price, so heat per added unit needs explicit modeling.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Drawdown-Scaled De-Risking (20% unit cut per 10% DD)
mechanism: Reducing unit size arithmetically during drawdowns counters the exponential path toward ruin and preserves capital so a recovery trend can be captured with full size restored.
setup_summary: For every 10% equity drawdown from peak, cut unit risk by 20% (2.0% -> 1.6% -> 1.28% ...). Restore unit size progressively as equity recovers. Example: down 11% -> trade 1.6% units; down 22% -> 1.28% units.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: account drawdown crosses each 10% threshold. Rule reverses (re-increase) only when equity starts recovering toward peak.
risk_geometry: Equity-based position de-leveraging ladder; a pure risk-management overlay on top of the entry/exit system.
quote: For every 10 percent in drawdown in their account, Turtles cut their trading unit risk by 20 percent. ... If their trading capital dropped down 22 percent, then they would cut their trading size by another 20 percent (1.6 × 80%), making each unit 1.28 percent.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'The Rules', Risk of Ruin (pp. 92-93)
notes: Directly portable to V8's RiskGate as a drawdown-scaled sizing ladder. Especially important under perp leverage where drawdowns accelerate via liquidation; the rule is falsifiable (compare fixed-2% vs de-leveraged sizing on the same tape).
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: System One Winner-Skip Filter (take breakouts after losses)
mechanism: Breakout signals cluster: consecutive breakouts after a winning one are disproportionately false, while a breakout taken after a prior loss is more likely the real trend; S2 is the fail-safe for filtered-out moves.
setup_summary: Skip a 20-day (S1) breakout if the previous 20-day breakout signal was a winner (even if it was not taken); do take it if the previous signal ended in a 2N loss. The 55-day (S2) breakout remains mandatory and catches big trends the filter skipped.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: new 20-day breakout; filter uses outcome of the prior 20-day breakout signal. A skipped S1 breakout that keeps trending is re-entered on the S2 55-day breakout.
risk_geometry: Signal-selection filter only, no change to stop/target geometry; S2 entry is the fail-safe re-entry path.
quote: The Turtles ignored the System One four-week breakout signal if the last four-week breakout signal was a winner. ... if the trade before a current four-week breakout was a 2N loss, they could take the breakout.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'The Rules', System One and System Two (p. 72)
notes: Requires a 'prior signal outcome' feature (history feature group) tracking last breakout direction and result in N terms. Note the same book reports false breakouts are common (the Turtles accepted small losses on most breakouts), so the filter's edge is an empirical claim to test on crypto 1h, not a given.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Parameter Robustness (minor changes must not matter)
mechanism: A robust systematic rule's performance is flat across small parameter variations; if a one-day change in breakout length changes results materially, the system is fragile and overfit.
setup_summary: Use robustness as the acceptance test for V8 experts and their variants: changing S1 entry from 20 to 21 bars (or a parameter by ~5%) must not materially change OOS performance. If it does, reject the parameterization as overfit. The core edge was attributed to simple breakout/moving-average components (Parker: 'two-thirds of that is what drives our profits').
trigger_invalidation: A variant that passes on one parameter value but fails a neighborhood of values is quarantined as overfit rather than promoted.
risk_geometry: Design/test methodology for expert variants; interacts with V8's variant multiplicity rules.
quote: In reality, a minor change of a variable in any robust trading system should not cause significant performance changes. If it does, you are in trouble.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'The Rules' (p. 74)
notes: Directly actionable for V8's variant discipline: parameter/threshold changes are variants of one family, and this rule supplies the acceptance criterion (performance plateau, not point estimate). Mirrors the book's warning against fixating on '20 vs 21 days'.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Cross-sectional relative strength (buy strongest, sell weakest)
mechanism: Relative strength persists: the strongest market keeps outperforming while the weak one lags; fading the spread assumes a convergence that trend followers reject.
setup_summary: Over a rolling window, rank a basket of markets/assets by return; when asset A clearly outperforms asset B in the same complex (Walsh's example: beans up 10c, corn down 5c), go LONG the strongest and SHORT the weakest; hold while the relative-strength ordering persists. Falsifiable on any cross-asset basket at daily bars.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis dies when the relative-strength ordering flips or the spread collapses to zero; long leg starts underperforming the short leg.
risk_geometry: Book states only the entry logic and direction; stop/target not given. V8 would need its standard ATR stop, R-multiple target, expiry_bars, and frozen relative-strength refs.
quote: If beans are up 10 cents and corn is down five cents, we buy beans. Some people think to buy corn because it's going to catch up with beans. We take the opposite. We'd rather buy the commodity that's strongest and sell the one that's weakest.
chapter_anchor: Ch.13 'Second-Generation Turtles', Mark J. Walsh (pp.172-173)
notes: Requires a cross_market feature group (ranked momentum across instruments) which V8 does not yet have; single-instrument experts cannot express this. Cross-sectional momentum across crypto perps is testable on 24/7 data but majors are highly correlated and the short leg pays funding, so the spread edge is thinner than in commodities.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: New N-period high/low breakout trend entry ('buy the all-time high')
mechanism: trend_continuation: a market printing prices never seen before is treated as a confirmed trend, not overextension, because the empirical frequency favors continuation over exhaustion.
setup_summary: When close exceeds the highest high (or breaks the lowest low) of the prior N periods, enter with the trend at next bar; Abraham's version buys all-time-high regimes that make intuitive sellers uncomfortable. Falsifiable: does a new-window-high close predict continuation over the next M bars vs. random entries?
trigger_invalidation: Close trades back through the breakout reference level -> failed breakout; abort or flip thesis (interfaces with the failed_breakout family).
risk_geometry: Book restates no S1/S2 numbers in this part (those are in Part 1). V8 geometry: entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE, stop 2xATR below entry or below breakout ref, target R-multiple, expiry_bars per system variant.
quote: To buy crude oil at $55? That's a hard bet to do when it's never been to $56. Never in the history of the world has it been to $56 and you say, 'It hit $55 today, I'm buying it.'
chapter_anchor: Ch.13, Salem Abraham (p.184)
notes: Distinct from the existing trend_pullback (which buys pullbacks inside an uptrend) and from the DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest (which requires a retest). The specific donchian 20/55-day variants (S1/S2) belong to Part 1 under donchian_breakout; this finding is the generic new-high breakout concept. 24/7 crypto has no exchange gaps, so breakout entries are clean on BTCUSDT 1h.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Trend-following payoff profile: long flat/down stretches punctuated by rare large gains
mechanism: skew_expectation: trend systems have right-skewed monthly returns - most months small losses, occasional explosive trend months, and multi-year flat/down stretches - all inside long-horizon compounders.
setup_summary: Design expectation backed by the book's published 19-20 year CFTC-filed tables (Parker, Abraham, Shanks, DiMaria, Rabar, Seidler, Cheval, Eckhardt): expect extended multi-week/month drawdowns and flat periods (Abraham 1992 -10.50%, 2005 -10.95%; Parker 2001 -7.98% with only 4 positive months) interleaved with rare large months (Parker Jun-88 +32.42%; Abraham May-88 +32.34%, Jun-88 +71.99%).
trigger_invalidation: Not a trade setup; a calibration claim about family-level return distribution.
risk_geometry: None per-trade; the lesson is about portfolio/family-level drawdown tolerance and evaluation horizon.
quote: Their careers are concrete proof of what sticking with a system over the long haul can do for a trading account.
chapter_anchor: Appendix III 'Turtle Performance Data' intro (p.199) and Tables 3.1-3.3 (pp.200-202)
notes: Publishes real monthly return series, the strongest empirical content in this part. Informs V8 lifecycle design: heat caps and screening gates must not terminate a family during its normal losing phase; judge trend families on multi-year frozen-OOS horizons. Expected profile for BTCUSDT 1h trend families is the same right-skew.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Back-door breakdown acceleration (crowded-long support-break short)
mechanism: After an euphoric, high-volume trend with one-sided (long) crowding, a break of support triggers a crowded exit ('the exit door is going to get awfully small') that accelerates the decline.
setup_summary: On BTC 1h: strong uptrend with rising volume, funding-rate crowding long, and overextension; place a short entry just below each defined support level. Thesis: if support is broken, price accelerates lower rather than drifting; if it holds, no harm (the position is an out-of-the-money 'landmine').
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close below a support level that was established during the euphoric phase. Invalidation: support holds and close reclaims above it; no acceleration within the forecast window; crowding unwinds without cascade (funding normalizes, no liquidation flush).
risk_geometry: Entry: below support (bar-close or stop-style entry, 'just below each support level'); stop: above the broken support / recent swing; target: accelerated continuation (unbounded in options; perp uses fixed-R or structure target); expiry: short forecast horizon because time decay is the enemy of the long-vol thesis.
quote: If the support lines are broken, the price will accelerate lower, and he places a back door put backspread just below each support level.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8 Investment Objectives, 'Special Situations' / Back Door Backspreads, pp. 240-241
notes: Crypto-native proxies for the 'everybody is long' condition: funding rate, long/short account ratios, open interest spikes. The cascade is directly testable with perp liquidation data. Requires the participation/flow feature group that is not yet formalized in V8.
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: Zone-capped deceleration trade (ratio-spread forecast structure)
mechanism: Price decelerates at support/resistance and congestion zones; a slow directional move into a capped target area (with declining vol) is a fading/short-vol opportunity rather than a trend opportunity.
setup_summary: On BTC 1h: slow, grinding directional move into a defined resistance/congestion zone (upside case) or support zone (downside case) with declining realized/implied volatility and weak momentum; fade the move expecting deceleration inside the zone, with the zone as the forecast target anchor.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: grinding approach into the zone with decaying momentum/vol. Invalidation: the boundary is penetrated (the 'lines in the sand' are crossed) or price velocity/magnitude exceeds the forecast, in which case the forecast is wrong and the position must be modified or exited immediately.
risk_geometry: Entry: on approach into the zone (limit/close); stop: beyond the zone boundary; target: the opposite side / zone center (option strike math gives max profit at the short strike); expiry: expiration cycle that expires before the projected end of the slow period ('when in doubt, use the expiration cycle that expires before the projected end').
quote: His forecast was for a slow, directional move toward a target area. Hopefully, the target area is capped by a resistance level or a congestion zone above the current underlying price...
chapter_anchor: Ch. 7 Trade Management, pp. 217-218
notes: The ratio spread itself is short-options (no perp analog), but the underlying forecast discipline — deceleration at S/R with declining vol — is the testable claim. This is a fade-at-zone hypothesis distinct from V8's trend-continuation experts.

strategy_name: Crowding-extreme contrarian (what-if reversal positioning)
mechanism: When participation is overloaded in one direction (overly bullish in an uptrend, overly bearish in a downtrend), the trend is fragile and reversal can be explosive; extremes are a trigger for low-cost contrarian 'what-if' positions.
setup_summary: On BTC 1h/4h: compute a crowding composite (funding rate, long/short ratio, OI growth, media/consensus tone) at trend extremes; when it exceeds a high threshold in the direction of the prevailing trend, stand ready for reversal plays (short after euphoric longs, long after capitulatory shorts) — 'what-if' positions placed like landmines in price zones that would trigger volatility.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: crowding extreme (e.g., funding above high percentile, extreme long/short ratio) concurrent with price at a zone. Invalidation: crowding persists while trend continues (no reversal within horizon); the extreme is followed by more trend, not a snapback.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit/close in the trigger zone with bounded risk (the book uses defined-risk backspreads); stop: beyond the trigger zone; target: reversion to the mean/extreme opposite; expiry: short horizon (long-vol thesis decays).
quote: Bullish consensus figures, VIX readings, put/call ratios, media chatter, and so on can be good indicators that market participants are getting either too optimistic or pessimistic.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8 Investment Objectives, Special Situations, p. 241
notes: Directly transferable: funding rate is a high-frequency, point-in-time crowding measure unique to perps (no VIX/put-call on-chain for BTC in 2009). Proposes a new feature-group input (participation/flow) feeding reversal candidates — complements rather than duplicates the existing 3 active experts.

strategy_name: Consolidation/continuation breakout in direction of prior trend
mechanism: A consolidation that forms after a trend and breaks out in the direction of that prior trend (continuation pattern) precedes resumption; the breakout itself is the high-velocity event to trade.
setup_summary: On BTC 1h: identify an established trend, then a tight, low-volume consolidation (flag/continuation pattern) against it; a breakout of the consolidation in the direction of the prior trend triggers continuation entry with a target equal to the pre-consolidation range projection.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close beyond the consolidation boundary in the trend direction. Invalidation: breakout fails and price re-enters the consolidation (failed breakout — reenter the range); no follow-through within the forecast horizon.
risk_geometry: Entry: breakout bar close; stop: opposite side of the consolidation (short strike 'backstopped by support or resistance'); target: prior-move extension / acceleration zone; expiry: matched to forecast breakout time.
quote: Consolidation pattern: An area pattern that breaks out in the direction of the previous trend (also called a continuation pattern).
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8 Concept Review, p. 223; Investment Objectives, pp. 239-240
notes: Corroborates V8's DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family (same continuation mechanism; the book adds the continuation-pattern framing and the short-strike-backstop placement rule). Kept DEFER_GATED until a derivatives tape exists, per the existing registry status.

strategy_name: Directionless-market regime filter (sideways suppresses directional experts)
mechanism: When the market is identified as directionless — price decelerating at defined support/resistance with low/declining volatility — the correct posture is limited-risk range/mean-reversion structures; directional trend plays have poor risk-reward.
setup_summary: Regime filter over the active expert set: classify the 1h BTC state as range/directionless when price repeatedly decelerates at S/R zones (boundaries respected) and realized vol is contracting; in that regime, suppress trend-continuation experts (trend_pullback, failed_breakout, liquidity_sweep_reclaim have reduced thesis validity) and let range/mean-reversion candidates (supply_demand_zone) take priority.
trigger_invalidation: Range regime invalidated when a boundary is penetrated (the 'lines in the sand' cross) or a breakout with velocity occurs; regime flips back to trending.
risk_geometry: N/A — regime gating, applied before risk admission; per-expert still_valid conditions remain active within the filter.
quote: Butterflies, condors, and their iron equivalents are limited-risk strategies that can be used during sideways or consolidating markets.
chapter_anchor: Appendix, Final Exam Part II, Scenario 5, p. 262; Ch. 7 Quiz, p. 220
notes: V8 currently has no regime gate (rule 14 keeps shared components ABSENT). This finding proposes the simplest possible form — a per-expert thesis-suppression based on range detection — as a refinement input, not a shared ranker, so it respects the complexity budget.

strategy_name: COT Movement Index rate-of-change surge
mechanism: The RATE of change of positioning toward an extreme marks when a counter-trend reaction has exhausted itself; a surge that then fails to restart the prevailing trend is a regime-change alert.
setup_summary: Weekly: Movement Index = COT Index(t) - COT Index(t-6 weeks). A +40 point buying surge during a correction in an uptrend marks the end of the pullback (re-buy); a -40 point selling surge during a bounce in a downtrend marks the end of the reaction (re-sell). If a +/-40 point surge fails to restart the prevailing trend, expect a major trend change - this is the signal's most valuable mode.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: +/-40 points in a 6-week window while a counter-trend reaction is underway. Invalidation: the surge does not resume the prevailing trend - that failure is itself the tip-off to a major trend change (e.g., pound rallying straight through a -40 point reading ended the major downtrend).
risk_geometry: No stop/target stated. Signals time entries in the direction of the prevailing trend; in flat ranges +/-40 signals replace COT climaxes as the useful trigger. Wang 2003's 1-standard-deviation net-position-change rule is the statistical analog and generates a high percentage of simultaneous signals.
quote: A ±40 point surge in the COT Index within a six-week period frequently marks the end of a counter-trend price reaction.
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, COT Movement Index, pp. 75-81
notes: The +/-40 point / 6-week threshold is a practitioner heuristic (cross-validated by Wang 2003's 1-sigma rule), and it needs a weekly positioning series that crypto does not natively have; funding/OI rate-of-change could stand in but the weekly cadence and commercial proxy are both weak.

strategy_name: Fund capacity exhaustion breakout failure
mechanism: Trend-following funds fuel breakouts; when their net long is already at its record/prior capacity while price retests a prior high, there is insufficient remaining speculative buying power to force a breakout, so the retest fails.
setup_summary: Weekly: price approaches its prior high while the large-speculator (fund) net position has already matched its prior record net long - i.e., buying capacity reached its previous limit. Expect the breakout to fail. The entry is not at the failed high but on the break below the prior reaction trough (support), once it is obvious funds are not buying and are liquidating.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: fund net long at its prior-high capacity while price retests the high. Invalidation: fund net position shows it has NOT exhausted buying capacity (new buying power available) - then a breakout attempt may succeed; also a lack of buying INTEREST (not capacity) can fail a breakout, which is less predictable.
risk_geometry: Entry on break below prior support trough (swing point); the failed-breakout top itself is not the entry level; book implies stop above the failed high.
quote: If a breakout relies on speculative buying (and most do), fund net positions can tip off their remaining buying power.
chapter_anchor: Ch 5, Net Positions, pp. 47-61 (Figure 5.7)
notes: Directly refines V8's existing failed_breakout family (liquidity_vacuum_reentry): add a crowding-exhaustion precondition, proxied in crypto by funding-rate percentile + OI blow-off at highs. Crypto 1h is momentum-dominated, so a failed-breakout-with-positioning-exhaustion filter is falsifiable on the existing tape. Positive-feedback-fund premise is literature-supported (Ch 8 studies); the capacity-exhaustion prediction is chart-based inference.

strategy_name: Abrupt sentiment reversal regime rule
mechanism: A sudden 180-degree flip in the net position of the crowd that had been fueling the trend means the current trend has overshot; anticipate a reversal regardless of which direction the new signal points.
setup_summary: Weekly: after an extended move, the group that drove the trend reverses its net position sharply within one report (e.g., commercials swinging from record long to record short - the S&P 500 in 1987, NASDAQ in March 2000). Treat the current trend as suspect and anticipate reversal, even if the COT signal itself looks confusing or is directionally 'wrong'. Corollary: in an uptrend, the failure of a minor COT buy signal to rebound prices is a strong warning of a major downturn.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: abrupt net-position flip after an extended move, or a minor-trend-direction signal failure. Invalidation: the flip/signal produces follow-through (no reversal); the book stresses this is a warning to protect/exit existing trend exposure, not a standalone reversal entry.
risk_geometry: Used as a regime/turn warning: cut or hedge trend-direction exposure and stand ready to reverse with technical confirmation; no price-based stop/target given.
quote: When you see an abrupt reversal in trader sentiment, anticipate a reversal in the current price trend, regardless of the direction of the COT signal.
chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Chart Pattern Validation, p. 109 (NASDAQ top); Ch 9, pp. 101-103
notes: Transferable to V8's lifecycle machinery as a dead-thesis/regime rule: a sharp flip in the crowding proxy (funding sign flip, OI blow-off, long/short ratio reversal) after an extended 1h trend flags overshoot. In crypto the flip is often liquidation-driven (flush-and-recover), so the 'reversal' outcome is less certain than in COT data - hence MEDIUM, and the rule should gate risk, not force entries.

strategy_name: Two-MA crossover on fund COT Index (mechanical COT system)
mechanism: Trend-following speculators' positioning leads price; a mechanical two-moving-average crossover on the speculator net-position index generates trend-following entries from an external, non-redundant dataset.
setup_summary: Weekly COT data stamped to daily bars: fast MA of the large-speculator COT Index crossing above the slow MA = buy on next day's open; crossing below = sell short; the model is always in the market with no stop. Tested on 35 futures markets 2000-2007, all positive gross (best pair per market, ~14 trades/year). The author explicitly warns it is not trade-ready: no stop-loss, no statistical verification, and drawdowns would be excessive.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: MA cross on the fund COT Index. The model is always-in so has no invalidation; the binding constraints the book documents are (a) the 3-10 day release lag (results were only marginal on pre-2000 bimonthly/monthly data) and (b) the need for a stop-loss fail-safe and a backup trend-catch option when the COT signal never comes.
risk_geometry: Always-in, no stop - explicitly flagged as the system's flaw; entries/exits at the open of the day following the signal; no roll cost included.
quote: Although such a simple set of trading rules might not be very effective if applied to price, hypothetical performance is quite impressive when applied to the Commitments data.
chapter_anchor: Ch 9, View from the Pits, pp. 97-103
notes: Methodology lessons for V8: (1) an external positioning dataset can produce signals comparable to price-based ones - in crypto, funding/OI percentile series could feed a mechanical cross; (2) data release lag is the dominant backtest bias - crypto has no equivalent lag (real-time data), which changes the edge structure; (3) always-in trend systems without stops bleed in crypto's volatility; (4) mandatory gating signals can make you miss the few big moves that make a year's profit.

strategy_name: Containment breakout (pent-up speculative demand)
mechanism: When the counter-trend crowd must sell (or buy) aggressively just to hold a price inside a range, the effort itself signals pent-up speculative demand on the other side; once containment lifts, the breakout is explosive.
setup_summary: Weekly: a prolonged trading range in which the counter-side sustains persistent selling (or buying) pressure to hold the boundary - visible as extreme normalized positioning (COT pinned below 50%) and repeated failed breakout attempts. The tell: when the counter-side begins covering shorts and accumulating (a rate-of-change buying surge inside the range), anticipate a breakout of the opposite boundary. OJ 2005: a year of aggressive commercial selling to contain prices presaged an explosive speculative bull move.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: containment effort + a positioning rate-of-change surge by the counter-side inside the range. Invalidation: containment relaxes without a surge (no pent-up flip), or prices break on the containment side first; also, in a sideways market a COT selling climax before a breakout is the exit-long / consider-short signal.
risk_geometry: Book recommends buying with commercials near the range bottom (COT buying climax) so you are aboard for the breakout; exit longs on a selling climax before the breakout; retest of the broken boundary after breakout = additional entry opportunity (90% buying climax).
quote: The excessive commercial selling pressure here was really a sign of pent-up speculative demand.
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, COT Movement Index, Figure 7.4 (OJ 2005 trading range), pp. 78-79; Ch 14 gold sideways tactic p. 155
notes: Crypto ranges are frequently resolved by liquidation cascades rather than containment-then-breakout, and the 'who is containing' side is opaque without commercial segmentation. The mechanism is plausible and falsifiable if a containment proxy (sustained funding-rate pressure + range-bound volatility) is formalized, but it is chart-case-based in the book.

strategy_name: Fading small traders (rejected scheme)
mechanism: Claim: small traders are 'dumb money' and should be faded. Verdict: the small-trader (nonreportable) bucket is a mixed bag of small commercials and speculators whose composition varies by market and trend, often moves too little to signal, and is not published separately - so the naive fade is not robustly executable.
setup_summary: Rejected practice: take positions opposite the small trader net position. The book shows small-trader patterns are a 'real mishmash' - sometimes fund-like, sometimes fading the trend (2005-2007 example) - and the group's net position is often near-flat. Only in specific markets (livestock, where commercials dominate the small totals) does the small-trader net position show structure, and there it mirrors commercials (fade-able in the opposite sense) rather than acting as a reliable dumb-money fade.
trigger_invalidation: n/a - strategy rejected; any retail-positioning fade must first establish the composition of the retail proxy.
risk_geometry: n/a
quote: The small speculator may be the 'dumb money,' but he is not stupid enough to come out from hiding among commercials in the small trader category.
chapter_anchor: Ch 4, Fading Small Speculators and Other Half-Baked Schemes, pp. 39-45; Ch 5 Small Trader Patterns pp. 59-60
notes: The literature premise (small traders are net losers; Ch 8 studies) is supported, but the actionable fade rule is rejected on data-composition grounds. For crypto: exchanges publish retail long/short ratios and funding, which tempt naive retail fades; this finding argues those proxies must be validated for composition (who is actually in the bucket) before any fade behavior is formalized.

strategy_name: Trader-Group Behavioral Role Asymmetry
mechanism: the three COT groups play stable, opposite behavioral roles — commercials counter-trend (negative feedback), large speculators/funds momentum-follow (positive feedback), small traders are systematically wrong-sided — so a group's net position is only interpretable through its role
setup_summary: Build separate positioning features per trader group with role-appropriate semantics: fade commercials at climaxes (counter-trend/negative feedback), confirm trends with large-speculator fund net direction (momentum/positive feedback), and treat small-trader net positions as a contrary indicator (index: 'fading of small traders'). Academic support cited in the book: Houthakker 1957, Wang 2001/2003, Hartzmark 1987, Leuthold-Garcia-Lu 1994, Kearns & Manners 2004.
trigger_invalidation: N/A — feature construction. Caveat: classification can blur — commodity index traders are reported inside the commercial counts and distort 'hedger' semantics (pp. 34-36), and swap dealers hold large long index-replication positions.
risk_geometry: N/A
quote: positive feedback A trader that adds positions as the market moves favorably to existing positions (momentum or trend-following).
chapter_anchor: Glossary 'positive feedback'; Index 'Trading styles' (pp. 51-59); References (Wang 2003; Kearns & Manners 2004)
notes: Crypto perps lack trader-type classification; the retail-crowd-vs-smart-money split is cruder and observable only via funding-rate sign, open-interest concentration, and liquidation data — so role semantics must be inferred, not read off a report.

strategy_name: profit_target_at_prior_support_resistance
mechanism: price repeatedly stalls at established prior support/resistance; a pre-committed target at such a level plus holding through pullbacks captures the full trend move that emotion-based early exits would truncate
setup_summary: After entry in the direction of an established move, set the target at the next major prior S/R level (round number or a level that stopped price in multiple prior years), frozen before entry, and hold through adverse pullbacks until price reaches it. Exemplars: EUR/JPY long at 119.00 (a barrier hit in Jan 2002 that took 9 months to break) targeting 131.00 (stopped in 1997/1998/1999); GBP/USD long after FOMC targeting 1.8600, 470 pips away, 'I made up my mind before I took the trade.'
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade entered on a thesis (technical barrier + macro confluence) with a pre-frozen structure target. Invalidation: target level is broken and closed beyond it (thesis dead); until then, pullbacks are not invalidation — exiting early on fear was the documented error ('I had let my emotions ruin the trade').
risk_geometry: Entry: market (bar close). Stop: not specified beyond thesis invalidation (break of the support thesis). Target: structure level, not fixed R — 131.00 vs. entry 119.00 was ~12R of stated move; 1.8600 was 470 pips on a 40-pip quick scalp thesis. Expiry: months (two months to exit in the fable), no bar-based expiry.
quote: Ride your profits, Harry. That's the lesson here... I have a profit target at a previous level of support and resistance, where price stopped cold several times this year, and as recently as just a week ago... 470 pips away, but it can get there. I made up my mind before I took the trade.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'Craig's Ten-Million-Dollar Lesson' p.35-38; Ch. 8 p.63
notes: Refinement candidate for the existing trend_pullback / failed_breakout experts: both currently hardcode target_r 1.0 and expiry_bars 8, which this lesson argues truncates winners. A variant that replaces fixed-R targets with frozen structure targets (prior swing high/low, round number with multi-touch history) and extends expiry until the frozen target or thesis break is a legitimate family variant, not a new family. The frozen-ref discipline matches V8's 'still_valid' dead-thesis exit.

strategy_name: pyramiding_position_build
mechanism: scaling into a position in tranches on favorable pullbacks reduces entry risk versus all-in entry and lets confirmed winners compound; adding only to positions already in profit converts a small probe into a large winner
setup_summary: Initiate with a small position (the exemplar opened 5M EUR/JPY at 119.00), then add tranches on each favorable pullback (119.50, 120.00, ... building to 500M) as long as the position remains in profit, exiting only at the pre-planned structure target. The stated contrast: 'I took oversized positions... instead of building the position over time' was the mistake that followed.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: existing exposure in profit and price pulling back within the trend toward the frozen entry-thesis. Invalidation: thesis break (pair cannot hold above the support/entry thesis) — 'I couldn't buy the pair at 119.00 anymore! When I closed the big trade, I lost the right to hold the EUR/JPY at a super-duper discounted price.'
risk_geometry: Entry: market on pullback, tranche-by-tranche. Stop: thesis-level invalidation; the book never pyramids into a losing position. Target: single frozen structure target for the whole pyramid. Expiry: months; no bar expiry.
quote: I didn't put all my trading capital into the first position. Instead, I built it up over time... with any pullback, even slight ones, I added to the winning position... I bought more after that at 119.50. Five million more Euros worth. And then ten million more at 120.00.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'Craig's Ten-Million-Dollar Lesson' p.36-39
notes: Directly conflicts with V8 rule 16 (one active exposure per instrument/direction), so this must be a backlog candidate, not a live family: lifting rule 16 for a pyramiding variant would require a registry experiment beating the single-exposure baseline on frozen OOS. The mechanism is falsifiable in the V8 simulator (fill-at-close tranche adds on pullbacks, single frozen target), and the book's stated failure mode — re-opening at a worse price after closing a winner, then oversizing — is exactly the behavior the lifecycle ExposureBook should gate against.

strategy_name: Old resistance becomes support (polarity-flip retest)
mechanism: After a breakout through old resistance, the traders who sold there are either trapped (they bail out near break-even, becoming buyers) or too psychologically pained to sell at that price again, so the level's seller pool empties and old resistance acts as support on retest.
setup_summary: After price convincingly breaks a previously tested resistance and later returns to it, expect old resistance to hold as support: buy the retest. On 1h BTCUSDT: a level that stopped rallies 3+ times, a decisive close through it, then a pullback back to the level.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = retest of the flipped level after a decisive breakout. Thesis invalidated if price trades back decisively through the old level (the flip failed) or if the retest attracts no buying.
risk_geometry: Entry: retest at the flipped level; stop: just beyond the flipped level to the downside ('where the market shouldn't be'); target: continuation toward the next significant reference point; no expiry stated.
quote: Hence, old resistance becomes support, and old support becomes resistance for the same reasons.
chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'Support Becomes Resistance and Resistance Becomes Support', pp.162-163
notes: Supplies the causal mechanism (trapped-seller bail-out + seller-pool depletion) for the backlog breakout_retest family, currently DATA_BLOCKED with requires=location,volatility,history. Distinct from the range fade: this is trend-continuation after a breakout, not mean-reversion at the edge.

strategy_name: High-retrace-lower-high failure then break of prior low (distribution breakdown)
mechanism: When a second rally fails to exceed a prior high, buyers' expectations are disappointed; if price then penetrates the intervening swing low, disappointed bulls liquidate en masse and there is no one to buy from them, so price falls sharply.
setup_summary: Market makes new highs, sells off; on the second approach the rally fails to exceed or equal the prior high (lower high); entry once price penetrates the prior swing low between the high and the retrace. On 1h BTCUSDT: prior high, lower-high failure, then a bar close below the swing low.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = penetration of the prior swing low after a lower-high failure. Thesis invalidated if the second attempt makes new highs (buyers validated) or the swing low holds on repeated tests.
risk_geometry: Entry: on break of the prior low; stop: above the failed high / where the market shouldn't be; target: continuation until buyers re-enter at some 'cheap' reference point; no expiry stated.
quote: If prices penetrate that low, watch for buyers to bail out en masse. For them to get out of their position, who is going to buy it from them? ... Fall like a rock.
chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'High à Retrace à Rally to a Lower High', pp.163-164
notes: Directly corroborates and refines the formalized failed_breakout expert (SHORT, close below windowed prior high after a failed breakout) by adding the prior-swing-low breakdown trigger and the disappointed-expectation liquidation-cascade mechanism. HIGH perp applicability: high leverage turns the 'no buyers to absorb' step into liquidation cascades at the support break.

strategy_name: Trendline break continuation (balance-shift)
mechanism: A trend has a rhythm/flow sustained by imbalance between buyers and sellers; a break of the trendline signals the balance of forces has shifted, and the market tends to keep going in the direction of the break.
setup_summary: In an established trend with a clear trendline and a recognizable ebb-and-flow rhythm, a decisive close beyond the trendline signals a balance shift; enter in the break direction. On 1h BTCUSDT: a multi-day trendline with at least 3 touches broken by a bar close beyond it.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = break beyond the significant trendline. Thesis invalidated if the break stalls and price returns through the trendline (the balance shift did not gain hold) or if no follow-through appears.
risk_geometry: Entry: pre-placed order at the price that would confirm the balance change; stop: 'where the market shouldn't be' (just beyond the trendline); target: trend continuation; no expiry stated.
quote: markets that break trendlines have a tendency to keep on going in the direction of the break, because it signals a significant shift in the balance of forces.
chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'Trends and Trendlines', pp.162-163
notes: Book itself cautions 'trends are a function of time' and the rhythm is a session ebb-and-flow concept; in 24/7 perp crypto the rhythm is weaker and trendlines are noisier, though the balance-shift logic is the same mechanism behind many crypto trend-break continuations. Corroborated across the library's trend-following books.
book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

strategy_name: Aggressor conviction: paying up to buy / selling below last price initiates momentum
mechanism: A trader willing to buy above the last price or sell below it has stronger conviction than the passive side; aggressive initiative makes the last price a new bottom/top, forces prior losers to liquidate, and can gather momentum.
setup_summary: When trades occur beyond the last posted price (takers crossing the spread), treat it as conviction flow that can gather momentum: 'who is paying up to get in or get out?' In perps this is measurable as taker-buy vs taker-sell aggressor volume at the top of the book.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = sustained aggressive buying/selling (price bid/offered to new levels with insufficient counterparties). Thesis invalidated when the aggressor side's conviction runs out, the passive side takes the initiative, or momentum stalls at a significant reference point.
risk_geometry: Entry: momentum-following with the aggressive side (no precise entry type given); stop: below/above the aggressor's last defended level; no target or expiry stated.
quote: a trader willing to buy high or sell low instead of buy low or sell high has to have a stronger conviction in his belief in the future value... he is making the last price a bottom.
chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'The Psychology of Price Movement', pp.152-154
notes: The 'last price becomes a bottom/top' reference-point logic is directly observable in perp order books, but V8's canonical 1h-bar MarketState has no trade tape, so this is a feature-group input gated on tick/agg-trade data (derivatives tape), not an active expert. Mechanism also underlies the failed_breakout and liquidity_sweep_reclaim experts.

strategy_name: Go with the flow: align with the dominant force until the balance shifts
mechanism: Prices move in the direction of the greatest force - traders fulfilling their beliefs about future value; identifying and aligning with the dominant side, then re-aligning when significant reference points show the balance shift, is the easiest way to make money.
setup_summary: Identify which side is establishing dominance (who is paying up, who is passive and liquidating); trade with that side; when price reaches significant reference points where the dominant side could be disappointed, watch for the balance to shift and re-align with the new dominant side.
trigger_invalidation: Alignment invalidated when the dominant force loses conviction at a significant reference point (sellers return in force / buyers stop paying up) and the balance shifts; the book's Step Five question set (who is paying up, how much strength, is momentum building, what would disappoint the predominate force) is the monitoring protocol.
risk_geometry: No mechanical entry/stop/target given; principle-level guidance.
quote: The greatest number with the strongest belief will always be right. The easiest way to make money is to go with the flow.
chapter_anchor: Ch.16 'Step Five: Learning to Think in Probabilities', pp.177-179
notes: Foundational trend-following rationale, heavily corroborated across the library's trend-following corpus. In V8 terms it supports the regime/flow filter concept and the 'trade with the side that has established dominance' logic behind trend_pullback, rather than a standalone entry.

strategy_name: Hammer / Hanging-man long-shadow reversal
mechanism: a long lower shadow with a tiny body at the range top shows sellers failed to hold the low; the same line is bullish or bearish purely by trend context
setup_summary: On the chosen timeframe, a bar has (1) real body at the upper end of the range, (2) lower shadow at least twice the body height, (3) no or very short upper shadow. After a downtrend this is a bullish hammer (bottom reversal); after an uptrend the identical line is a bearish hanging man (top reversal) that REQUIRES next-bar confirmation (open below the hanging-man's real body, or a black close below its close). Confidence scales with shadow length / smallness of body; white hammer body slightly more bullish, black hanging-man body slightly more bearish.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: hammer/hanging-man shape in a defined trend. Hanging man invalidated if next bar opens higher / gaps up (book: 'if the market opens lower the next day, those who bought... are now left hanging'); hammer invalidated if bears make new lows without reclaiming (hammer 4 case in Ch.4).
risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close (book Ch.1: patterns complete on the close). Stop: 'the hammer's low could be used as a protective stop out level' (stated for trendline-test hammer, Ch.11) or under the support line. Target: not stated in book - use structure/opposite trend. No expiry.
quote: The longer the lower shadow, the shorter the upper shadow and the smaller the real body the more meaningful the bullish hammer or bearish hanging man.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 'Reversal Patterns - Hammer and Hanging-Man Lines' pp.28-38
notes: Single most falsifiable candlestick rule in the book (three crisp criteria + confirmation requirement) and it is the closest candlestick cousin to V8's liquidity_sweep_reclaim (the hammer's lower shadow IS a wick through a low that gets reclaimed). strategy_name: Doji after a rally (top-calling indecision with bottom asymmetry)
mechanism: a session that opens and closes at the same price signals buyer indecision; an uptrend needs buyer conviction to persist, so doji breaks the scaffolding; in downtrends a falling market can continue by its own weight so doji loses reversal power
setup_summary: A doji (open==close within a few ticks) after a long white candle in an uptrend - especially after a prolonged/overbought rally - warns of a top; the more conservative the trader, the more confirmation is required (next black candle, hanging man, or long black session). Falsifiable asymmetry claim: 'as good as doji are at calling tops... they tend to lose reversal potential in downtrends' - doji need more confirmation to signal a bottom than a top. Doji shadows can become support/resistance; doji are only meaningful in markets where doji are not already frequent (do not use intra-day charts under 30 minutes).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: doji (or near-doji at an important junction) after an uptrend. Invalidation: no confirming follow-through; a doji at the middle of a trading band or in doji-dense markets is noise; doji star bearishness negated if the next bar gaps higher.
risk_geometry: Entry: on confirmation bar close. Stop: beyond the doji extreme or below the supporting trendline. Target: structure-based. No expiry.
quote: Yet, as good as doji are at calling tops, based on experience, they tend to lose reversal potential in downtrends.

The 'doji becomes support/resistance' idea feeds the location feature group. The near-doji tolerance ('a few ticks') needs a volatility-relative (ATR) threshold in V8, not an absolute tick.

strategy_name: Windows (gaps) as continuation, support/resistance, and pullback magnets
mechanism: a gap in the direction of the trend marks a discontinuity in available supply/demand; corrections are expected to travel back to the window, which then acts as a floor or ceiling
setup_summary: A window is a gap between the prior and current session's price extremes. In an uptrend a window implies further rise and should be a floor on pullbacks: 'corrections go back to the window', so buy pullbacks into the window while it holds. If the window closes and selling pressure continues after the close, the prior uptrend is voided (and vice versa for downtrends). Corollaries: windows from a congestion zone or a new high deserve special attention; three windows in one trend imply a top/bottom is near (especially with a turning-point candle after the third); a window in a rising market not closed within three days predicts a rally.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: window formed in a trending market; pullback into the window holds. Invalidation: window closes AND opposite-direction pressure continues through it (trend voided) - the book's Dow-crash example required both closing the window AND continuation of buying force.
risk_geometry: Entry: on pullback into the window (buy zone) / short into window-as-resistance. Stop: under/over the window. Target: not stated (trend resumption). No expiry.
quote: Traditional Japanese technical analysis (that is, candlesticks) asserts that corrections go back to the window.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 7 'Continuation Patterns - Windows' pp.119-129
notes: True price gaps are structurally rarer in 24/7 perps than in the 1990s futures this book covers, which caps applicability at MEDIUM. But the window concept survives in crypto as daily/weekly-candle gaps and as the 'fair-value gap / imbalance' level that price retests - the pullback-to-window behavior is observable. strategy_name: Morning/evening star and doji-star (three-bar gap-stalemate reversal)
mechanism: a star (small body not overlapping the prior body) represents a deadlock in the bulls-vs-bears tug of war; the prior trend's power has dissipated and the market is vulnerable to reversal once the third bar confirms
setup_summary: Three-bar patterns: morning star (bottom) = tall black body, small body gapping lower (star), then a white body closing well within the first bar's black body; evening star (top) = mirror with black third bar intruding into the first white body. Doji stars (star is a doji) are more potent but demand next-session confirmation; a doji star in an uptrend is negated if the following session gaps higher. Evening star needs only the star's body low above the first body high (weaker requirement than a Western island top). Factors: gaps before/after the star, third bar closes deeply into first body, light volume on bar 1 and heavy on bar 3.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pattern completion (third bar close well into the first body). Invalidation: no confirmation the session after a doji star; doji-star bearishness voided if next bar gaps higher white; third-bar white that closes only shallowly into the first black body (on-neck/in-neck/thrusting) is bearish not bullish.
risk_geometry: Entry: after third-bar completion (close-confirmed). Stop: beyond the pattern's extreme (e.g., under the morning star's low). Target: not stated. No expiry.
quote: The star's small real body represents a stalemate in the tug of war between the bulls and bears.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'Stars' pp.55-70 (Morning Star p.56, Evening Star p.59, Doji Stars p.64, Shooting Star p.70)
notes: The star's defining feature is a body that does NOT overlap the prior body - in continuous 24/7 trading this 'gap-away' condition is less frequent than in gapping futures/equities, hence MEDIUM. The load-bearing, crypto-robust core is the third-bar-close-deeply-into-first-body confirmation gate, which is fully observable on 1h bars. strategy_name: Oscillator divergence (RSI/stochastics) with trend-conditional use
mechanism: price making new extremes while momentum (RSI/stochastics) fails to confirm shows the move is internally weak; divergence warns the trend is stalling
setup_summary: Negative/bearish divergence: price at a new high while the oscillator does not make a concurrent high (more meaningful when the oscillator is in overbought territory, RSI>70/80). Positive/bullish divergence: price at a new low while the oscillator prints a higher low. Entry requires confirmation: RSI moving back above its prior high, slow %K crossing back above %D (book's two-step stochastic rule: oversold <=25 for %D + positive divergence + %K crossing %D). Hard directional gate from the book: use oscillator signals only in the direction of the dominant trend; 'overbought markets usually should not be shorted' - overbought is a defense signal for longs, not a short trigger.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence in an overbought/oversold region with a crossover/confirmation signal. Invalidation: price keeps making records (divergence without confirmation is only a warning); a new major trend starting from a congestion-breakout can keep the oscillator pinned overbought.
risk_geometry: Entry: on the confirmation crossover or a coincident candlestick signal (the book shows candlesticks can give the signal a few days earlier than RSI confirmation alone). Stop: beyond the recent swing extreme. Target: not stated. No expiry.
quote: Do not short on a bearish oscillator signal unless the prevailing trend is heading south.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 14 'Candlesticks with Oscillators' pp.227-236 (RSI pp.228-232, Stochastics pp.232-234)
notes: The trend-gate rule (oscillator signals only with the dominant trend; overbought is not a short trigger) is the anti-naive-mean-reversion lesson and aligns with V8's behavior-driven design: divergence is a trend-stall warning, not an unconditional reversal. strategy_name: Trend-context filter and confluence requirement for candlestick signals
mechanism: a pattern's meaning is conditional on the dominant trend; single-pattern signals without independent confirmation are weak
setup_summary: Candlestick signals are only actionable in the direction of the prevailing higher-timeframe trend (a bullish hammer in a bear market is not a buy; a bullish signal in a bull market, especially confirmed by an independent oscillator/volume signal, is a buying point). Reversal patterns are also context-conditional (doji is more significant as a top than a bottom).
trigger_invalidation: N/A - this is a gating methodology, not a tradeable setup. V8 should apply it as a regime/admission filter before any single-pattern setup is allowed to emit.

strategy_name: Oscillator divergence (price extremes not confirmed by momentum) with candlestick confirmation
mechanism: when price makes a new extreme but momentum does not, the driving force is decelerating, so the trend is at risk
setup_summary: Price prints a new low (high) while stochastics/RSI/momentum print a higher low (lower high) - a positive (negative) divergence; when a candlestick bottoming (topping) signal (hammer, dark-cloud cover, evening star) appears in the same zone, the prior trend is treated as ended. Exhibits: S&P 1990 stochastics divergence at hammer cluster; gold momentum divergence at long-legged doji.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence extreme + candlestick reversal in the same zone. Invalidated if price prints a further new extreme without a reclaiming close (divergence persists but trend resumes).
risk_geometry: Entry on confirmation bar close; stop beyond the divergence extreme (swing low/high); target = prior range or polarity level. Book gives no fixed R-multiples.
quote: If prices reach new highs and stochastics do not, this is a negative divergence and is bearish. If prices establish new lows and stochastics do not, this is a positive divergence and is bullish.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 14 'Candlesticks with Oscillators' (Exhibits 14.5-14.8, pp. 232-239); Glossary B 'Divergence'

Caveat for crypto: divergences are frequent in hard-trending perps and the book itself only treats them as meaningful with the candlestick confirmation - so the divergence alone is a weak feature; the confirmed variant is the backlog candidate.

strategy_name: Oscillator overbought/oversold extreme with candlestick confirmation
mechanism: at market-specific oscillator extremes, continuation is unlikely; a candlestick reversal at the extreme raises the odds of a top/bottom
setup_summary: When momentum/stochastics reach a market-specific overbought (heating-oil example: 10-day momentum ~+200) or oversold (~-400) level, the market should stall or back off; the odds of a reversal increase if a bearish (evening star, harami cross) or bullish (hammer) candlestick pattern appears at the same extreme. Stochastics: a %K/%D cross from under 25% is a stronger signal.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: oscillator extreme + candlestick reversal in the same zone. Invalidated if the oscillator re-extends to a new extreme with price following (extreme levels are sticky, so a level alone is not a signal).
risk_geometry: Entry on candlestick confirmation close; stop beyond the extreme swing; target = retracement of the prior move. No fixed R-multiples stated.
quote: At the 200-point overbought level, continuation of the prior rally is unlikely and the market should either trade sideways or backoff. The odds of a top reversal with an overbought momentum reading are increased if there is bearish candlestick confirmation.

strategy_name: Open-interest trend confirmation, high-OI stop cascade, and trapped-longs supply
mechanism: rising OI shows new participants financing the move; falling OI during a rally means short covering; unusually high OI at highs turns stop-losses into a cascade and traps late longs as future supply
setup_summary: (1) Rising OI confirms the trend (new longs aggressive in up-moves, new shorts in down-moves); a rally on declining OI is short covering and vulnerable. (2) Unusually high OI coinciding with new price highs presages trouble: sell-stops clustered along the advance trigger a chain-reaction cascade once price turns (sugar 1990), and longs who survived are trapped overhead, so any rally meets their exit supply.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger for the cascade: OI at unusual highs concurrent with new price highs. Invalidated if OI rolls over before price breaks (bears exit first) or if price keeps making highs on still-rising OI (genuine new-money trend).
risk_geometry: N/A - flow/participation feature; the cascade leg is a short-side timing input and a risk flag for existing longs.
quote: If there is unusually high open interest coinciding with new price highs it could presage trouble... a chain reaction of triggered sell stop loss orders can cause a cascade of prices.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 15 'Candlesticks with Volume and Open Interest' (pp. 248-251, cotton and sugar exhibits)
notes: Open interest is published in real time for crypto perps; the stop-cascade mechanism maps directly to liquidation cascades (the perp-native version of this). The 'trapped longs in pain become rally supply' element is an overhead-supply/positioning feature, analogous to the existing flow vocabulary. Doji clusters at the OI plateau top (sugar, bonds) provide the candlestick confirmation leg.

strategy_name: Candlestick reversal signals as volatility-regime timing
mechanism: a candlestick 'truce' reversal in a strong trend at high volatility marks the shift from trend to lateral, hence volatility contraction; a reversal at low volatility in a range forecasts a new trend with volatility expansion
setup_summary: In a strong trend that has pushed volatility unusually high, a candlestick reversal indicating a bull/bear truce (harami, counterattack lines, doji after a long white body) flags the end of the trend and an expected volatility contraction. Conversely, a candlestick reversal at low volatility in a lateral band flags a new trend and rising volatility. The author notes the shifts are shorter-term, and that signals work better against historic than implied volatility.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: reversal pattern at a high-vol trend extreme (or low-vol range). Invalidated if the trend resumes and volatility keeps expanding.
risk_geometry: N/A - regime/feature signal; could inform a volatility regime filter in V8 or the simulator's vol modeling.
quote: If a strong trending market has pushed volatility levels to unusually high levels, the emergence of a candlestick reversal indicator may provide an attractive time to sell volatility or to offset a long volatility trade.

notes: The contraction-after-truce claim is a falsifiable volatility feature: expected-vol decline conditioned on a reversal pattern at a high-vol trend extreme. Implied vol requires an options chain (Deribit) which V8's perp data does not include; realized/historic vol is directly computable, and the author explicitly says candlesticks work better with historic vol.
