strategy_name: Window (gap) continuation - 'the market goes to the window'
mechanism: an unfilled window in the direction of the trend acts as a magnet: price pulls back to it, the window holds as support/resistance, and the trend resumes
setup_summary: A window (gap) opens in the direction of the trend; price is expected to pull back to the window, which acts as support (up-gap) or resistance (down-gap), then the trend resumes. In the author's trades the window is used as a continuation leg and as a stop reference (crude: short with stop slightly above the June 15-18 window at $17.65, target retest of the hammer lows; coffee: failure to clear the window's resistance area triggered the short).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pullback into an open window in the trend direction. Invalidated if the window is filled (closed) and price continues through it - the support/resistance premise is dead.
risk_geometry: Entry on rejection at the window edge; stop beyond the window's far edge (author: stop slightly above the window high); target = retest of the prior extreme (hammer lows).
quote: When the market rallies and opens a window, there should be a pullback to that window. The window should be support... The Japanese expression is that 'the market goes to the window.'

strategy_name: No-trade patience and market-mood regime selection
mechanism: profitability comes partly from not trading; forcing trades when price action is not aligned with the current market mood (trending vs drifting/choppy vs transition) degrades edge
setup_summary: Naked trading spends most of its time waiting for price to reach strong zones; each catalyst (kangaroo tail, last kiss, big shadow, trendy kangaroo) is suited to a particular market mood. Falsifiable test offered: back-test one year of a high-frequency setup on a short timeframe and a low-frequency setup on a long timeframe and compare profitability; when neither setup is present, the correct action is no trade.

strategy_name: Last Kiss breakout-retouch confirmation
mechanism: True breakouts retouch the broken zone and hold; fake-outs snap back inside the box, so entry is deferred until a retouch plus a continuation candle in the breakout direction.
setup_summary: Identify a consolidation box (support + resistance zones, at least two touches on each side). Wait for price to break beyond one zone, then wait for the market to return and retouch the box edge; enter via a buy/sell stop beyond the high/low of the first strong candle in the breakout direction printed at the retouch. Emergency stop at the midpoint of the box (support + box width/2); if a candle closes back inside the box the thesis is dead and the trade is exited. Target = nearest zone.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: breakout beyond one zone, retouch of the box edge, strong directional candle at the retouch. Invalidation: any close back inside the box exits (usually a smaller loss than the emergency stop); emergency stop at box midpoint.
risk_geometry: Entry: stop order beyond the retouch candle extreme (buy stop above high for up-breaks, sell stop below low for down-breaks). Emergency stop = midpoint of consolidation box. Dead-thesis exit: close back inside the box. Target: nearest zone. No fixed expiry stated.
quote: the last-kiss trade is based on the retouch principle. The market will often come back to a significant zone once the market has expanded beyond the zone
chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'The Last Kiss' — retouch principle pp.82-93 (rules p.92-93)

strategy_name: Wammie/Moolah double-touch zone reversal
mechanism: Two touches on a zone with a higher low (or lower high) and enough separation show momentum dying out; the second touch failing to extend the zone test flips the balance toward reversal.
setup_summary: Double bottom (wammie) on a support zone where the second touch is HIGHER than the first, with at least 6 candles between touches; enter on the first strong bullish candle at the second touch via a buy stop above its high; stop below the first (lower) touch; target the next zone. Moolah is the mirror: double top with a lower second touch, sell stop below the bearish candle at the second touch, stop above the first touch, target the next zone below.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: two distinct zone touches with a higher low (wammie) / lower high (moolah), >= 6 bars between touches, strong candle on the second touch. Invalidation: stop beyond the first touch; fewer than 6 bars between touches implies the market is coiling for a breakout THROUGH the zone (do not trade).
risk_geometry: Entry: buy stop above the strong bullish candle at the second touch (wammie) / sell stop below the bearish candle (moolah). Stop: a few pips beyond the first touch — deliberately placed so a third touch of the zone does not stop the trade. Target: next zone. No expiry stated.
quote: a wammie formation is identified by a second touch that is higher than the first touch on the zone... A wammie trade is only valid if there are at least six candlesticks between the first and second touches.
chapter_anchor: Ch.7 'Wammies and Moolahs' pp.111-129 (characteristics pp.125-128, tips p.128-129)
notes: The six-bar separation rule is the distinctive falsifiable filter; rapid repeated touches signal imminent breakout rather than reversal. In leverage-driven crypto, zones break more often than in spot FX, so the higher-low/lower-high discriminator and the stop-behind-first-touch geometry are the load-bearing parts.

strategy_name: Trendy Kangaroo pause-breakout continuation
mechanism: In a strong trend, a tight 3-10 candle pause builds a minor zone; a kangaroo-style candle that sticks beyond the pause in the trend direction shows the pause is a rest stop, not a reversal.
setup_summary: During a strong uptrend (or downtrend) the market pauses with 3-10 candles in a tight consolidation; then a kangaroo-style candle prints with open/close in the extreme third and a tail that sticks out beyond the consolidation range in the trend direction. Enter via a stop beyond the candle's extreme in the trend direction; stop on the other side of the candle; target the next zone. Not ideal if printed right after a large correction (may signal trend end).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: established trend + small pause + kangaroo candle sticking beyond the pause range. Invalidation: stop on the other side of the candle; set-ups after a large correction may signal trend exhaustion; a candle that does not stick beyond the pause range is not valid.
risk_geometry: Entry: buy stop above the high (bullish) / sell stop below the low (bearish) of the trendy kangaroo. Stop: a few pips beyond the opposite extreme. Target: next zone. No expiry stated.
quote: The market pauses and several candlesticks print in a small consolidation range... A trendy kangaroo prints below the consolidation range.

strategy_name: Three-Bar trailing exit
mechanism: Trailing the stop behind the extreme of the last three closed bars locks in trend profit while giving the market a bounded cushion.
setup_summary: For a long, once three bars have closed the stop trails below the lowest low of the three most recent closed bars; for a short, above the highest high of the three most recent bars. The stop is adjusted only when a bar closes and never moves against the position. Works best when the market accelerates into a strong trend; in non-trending tape it exits for minimal profit (the book shows a 13-pip win).
trigger_invalidation: Applies from 3 bars after entry; stop adjusted at bar close only; exit when the trailing stop is hit.
risk_geometry: Trailing stop = lowest low / highest high of the last 3 closed bars plus a few pips. Candle must close before the stop moves. No target or expiry (pure trailing).
quote: the exit is based on the price action of the most recent three bars... the lowest low of the previous three candlesticks (for buy trades), or the highest high of the previous three candlesticks (for sell trades)

strategy_name: Setup-to-regime matching (choppy vs trending)

strategy_name: Trendline / Moving-Average Pullback Bounce
mechanism: A valid trend slope persists; a pullback that touches and bounces off the rising trendline (or MA support) is a continuation entry because buyers step in at proven support, and the more times the line is tested the more significant it is.
setup_summary: In a defined uptrend (rising peaks and troughs, price above an up trendline drawn under at least two rising reaction lows, preferably touched 3 times), buy when price pulls back to the trendline and closes back above it. Mirror in downtrends: short bounces to a falling down trendline. Same logic applies to moving-average support (e.g., close below 50-day warns of drop toward the 200-day). Falsifiable on 1h BTCUSDT by defining trendline support as a frozen line through prior reaction lows and entry on a confirming bar close.
trigger_invalidation: A decisive close below the up trendline (or below MA support) invalidates the bounce; in downtrends a decisive close above the falling trendline invalidates the short. Failure of price to hold a previously-tested trendline is itself an early reversal warning.
risk_geometry: Entry at bar close after the trendline touch; stop below the trendline or below the recent reaction low; target = prior high (resistance); no R-multiple or expiry stated (book trades from daily/weekly bar closes).
quote: Retests of up trendlines often present excellent buying opportunities.

strategy_name: Percentage / Fibonacci Retracement Entry (1/3, 1/2, 2/3)
mechanism: Corrections in a trend retrace predictable fractions of the prior move (min 1/3, typically 1/2, at most 2/3); support at these levels in an uptrend attracts resumption buying, while a move beyond two-thirds implies the correction is actually a full trend reversal.
setup_summary: Measure a completed swing (e.g., 20 to 40). In an uptrend, buy the pullback when price reaches the 50% retracement level (or the 38%-62% zone, commonly 38/50/62) of the prior advance and resumes higher; in a downtrend, sell bounces into the one-third-to-half retracement area. Levels act as support in uptrends and resistance in downtrends; a retracement beyond two-thirds switches the thesis to full reversal.
trigger_invalidation: A move beyond the two-thirds (66%) retracement level invalidates the continuation thesis and indicates a total trend reversal.
risk_geometry: Entry at the retracement level on a bar close; stop below the two-thirds level (or below the swing low); target = the prior extreme; no expiry stated. The book notes Fibonacci levels (38/62) derive from the Fibonacci number series.
quote: A stock that's traveled from 20 to 40 will often retrace about 10 points (50 percent) before resuming its advance.
chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'Retracing Our Steps by One-Third, One-Half, and Two-Thirds' (pp.34-37)
notes: Distinct mechanism from trendline pullback: structural percentage levels rather than a slope line. Fully computable on continuous crypto perp data; the two-thirds-overrun rule gives a clean dead-thesis condition. Corroborated widely in this library's TA canon.

strategy_name: Weekly Key-Reversal Bar
mechanism: A wide-range bar that opens with trend-extension (breaks a support level) and closes back through the prior week's range shows absorption of the losing side's flow (exhaustion), with width of the bar and heaviness of volume scaling significance.
setup_summary: On a weekly chart during a decline: the stock starts the week with heavy selling and breaks below a support level, then closes by week's end above the previous week's price range — an upside weekly reversal (LONG setup). Mirror: prices open the week sharply higher and collapse at week's end — a downside reversal (defensive/short). Wider weekly bar and heavier trading volume increase significance; more meaningful when occurring near historic support/resistance. Daily version = key reversal day but carries less weight.
trigger_invalidation: Book states the downside reversal 'isn't usually enough to turn the chart bearish' alone — it warrants defensive action, so treat as a caution signal pending confirmation rather than an immediate short.
risk_geometry: Entry on the weekly close (bar close); no explicit stop or target given; volume and range act as a strength filter.
quote: A stock starts the week with a lot of selling and usually breaks under some type of support level. By week's end, however, prices have turned dramatically upward and close above the previous week's price range.
chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'Weekly Reversals' (p.38)
notes: Weekly bars exist on 24/7 crypto (Sunday 00:00 UTC close) and the pattern is objectively definable (week open near lows, week close above prior week high). No gap mechanics on perps so 'breaks support' is a continuous move; volume data available, though wash-trading caveats apply.

strategy_name: Head-and-Shoulders Neckline Break
mechanism: After an extended trend, a final push beyond the prior extreme (head) flanked by two lower highs (shoulders) exhausts the driving side; a decisive close through the neckline (line through the intervening troughs) completes the reversal, with the head-to-neckline distance projecting a minimum move.
setup_summary: In an uptrend, price forms three peaks: two shoulders near the same level flanking a higher head; draw the neckline through the two intervening troughs. A decisive close below the neckline signals a new downtrend (target = neckline-break price minus head-to-neckline vertical distance). Mirror for the inverse head-and-shoulders bottom (three lows, middle lowest; upside neckline break = new uptrend). Volume/OBV should confirm the break.
trigger_invalidation: Pattern incomplete until neckline breaks; measurements are approximate minimums, not precise targets. Upside volume (heavier volume more critical on upside than downside) absent at the break weakens the signal.
risk_geometry: Entry at neckline break on bar close; stop above/below the neckline or at the head; target = pattern height projected from break point; no expiry stated. Book cites the NY Fed staff report (Osler & Chang 1995) that the pattern produces statistically and economically significant profits in currencies.
quote: The final conclusion of the report was that the head and shoulders pattern produces statistically and economically significant profits when applied to currency trading.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Head and Shoulders Pattern' and 'Even the Fed Is Charting' (pp.60-65)
notes: Only finding in this part with an explicit statistical citation (NY Fed Osler-Chang). Neckline break is objectively definable at bar close. Subjective identification risk (which swings are shoulders) argues for a tight formal definition if formalized.

strategy_name: Triangle Continuation Breakout
mechanism: Sideways consolidation between converging trendlines within an established trend is a pause; resolution usually occurs in the direction of the prior trend about two-thirds to three-quarters into the pattern, with the vertical height projecting the move.
setup_summary: After a trend, price narrows into a symmetrical triangle (each trendline touched at least twice, often three times); on a decisive break of one side in the direction of the prior trend (with volume pickup, especially on upside breaks), trade continuation. Ascending triangle (flat top, rising bottom) = bullish; descending triangle (flat bottom, falling top) = bearish. Target = triangle's widest height projected from the breakout point; the longer the pattern has formed, the more significant the move.
trigger_invalidation: Breakout that fails / price re-enters the pattern; an upside breakout not accompanied by a noticeable volume increase is immediately suspect.
risk_geometry: Entry on the bar-close break of the trendline; stop back inside the pattern (beyond the opposite line); target = projected height; pattern duration scales significance.
quote: Usually, about two-thirds to three-quarters of the way into the pattern, prices will break out in the direction of the prior trend.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'The Triangle' (pp.65-69)
notes: Continuation variant distinct from reversal patterns; overlaps starter vocabulary tight_consolidation / range_compression. No gaps on crypto perps remove gap-fill complications around consolidation ranges; volume confirmation available.

strategy_name: Volume / On-Balance-Volume Trend Confirmation and Divergence
mechanism: In a healthy trend volume flows with the trend (heavier on rallies than pullbacks); when price and volume/OBV diverge the trend is losing momentum, and OBV often breaks out before price, giving an early participation signal.
setup_summary: Confirm trend health: OBV line rising with price = healthy; price at new highs while OBV makes lower highs (or OBV falls) = negative divergence, warning the trend is in trouble. Volume rule: in a healthy uptrend volume bars are larger on up days and smaller on pullbacks; heavier volume on pullbacks than on rallies is an early warning. At important bullish breakouts a noticeable increase in volume is essential; an upside breakout without it is suspect. OBV line often breaks out before price does.
trigger_invalidation: Price and OBV/volume line diverging → treat trend as weakening; signal is a filter/reduction cue rather than an entry.
risk_geometry: Not an entry setup; acts as a confirmation/filter on entries and as an early-exit warning; no stops or targets stated.
quote: An upside breakout in any market that is not accompanied by a noticeable increase in trading activity is immediately suspect.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Volume Analysis' and 'Granville's On-Balance Volume' (pp.50-54)
notes: OBV and volume-based divergence are directly computable on perp/SL 1h data and belong in the participation feature group (marketstate). Caveat for crypto: reported volume can include wash/fake volume on some venues — prefer aggregated trusted-feed volume. This feature should also gate the backlogged breakout_retest family.

strategy_name: ADX Trend/Range Regime Filter
mechanism: The ADX line (derived from +DI vs -DI) classifies market mode: rising ADX = trending (favor trend-following tools), falling/flat ADX = range (favor oscillators); ADX>40 then dropping = trend exhaustion.
setup_summary: Compute +DI, -DI and ADX (Welles Wilder directional movement). ADX below 20 = low volatility, no trend (use nontrending/oscillator tools); ADX rising above 20 = beginning of an important trend (use trend-following); ADX well above 40 then starting to drop = trend exhausted, switch back to range tools. Use weekly ADX for primary regime determination (weekly more significant than daily).
trigger_invalidation: Regime classification flips when ADX direction reverses; the rule only selects which tool class to use, it does not by itself enter positions.
risk_geometry: None — a tool-selection filter (moving averages vs oscillators), not an entry/stop/target system.
quote: A rising ADX line tells us that a market is in a trending mode. A falling or flat ADX line reflects a trading range environment.
chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'The Average Directional Movement (ADX) Line' (pp.131-135)
notes: Directly implementable as a V8 regime gate on 1h BTCUSDT: gate which expert families (trend vs mean-reversion) are admissible per MarketState. ADX is a trend/volatility feature computed in marketstate; threshold params (20/40) become variants.

strategy_name: Stochastic Oscillator Reversal with Longer-Timeframe Trend Filter
mechanism: Oscillator extremes flag overextension; the fast-timeframe (daily) overbought/oversold cross is only traded in the direction the longer timeframe (weekly, then monthly) points, producing 'buy dips in uptrends, sell rallies in downtrends'.
setup_summary: Slow stochastics (14,3,3): %K = (close-low14)/(high14-low14)*100, %D = 3-period MA of %K. >80 overbought, <20 oversold. As long as weekly stochastic lines are positive (%K above %D), take only daily buy signals from oversold (<20) with %K crossing above %D (preferably with a positive divergence) and ignore daily sell signals; when weekly lines are negative, ignore daily buy signals and take daily overbought (>80) crosses for shorts. General rule: always use the next-longer timeframe (14h→14d→14w→14m) to set direction.
trigger_invalidation: Weekly stochastics flip against the open position; in strong running markets oscillator stays pinned >80/<20 and should not be faded; daily signals alone are premature (needs weekly confirmation).
risk_geometry: Entry on daily bar close after the cross; no explicit stop/target; book shows combined RSI+stochastic confirmation improves reliability (stochastics earlier but less reliable; wait for RSI 70/30 confirmation).
quote: always use the next longer time period to determine the direction of the market you will be trading from
chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'The Stochastics Oscillator' and 'Weekly Signals Determine Position' (pp.110-117)
notes: The multi-timeframe trend-filter principle is a core methodology lesson for V8 lifecycle: longest-admissible timeframe sets the exposure side. Stochastics computable on 1h bars; weekly/monthly candles form naturally on 24/7 data.

strategy_name: RSI Overbought/Oversold with Divergence and Failure Swing
mechanism: Price making new highs while RSI fails to confirm (divergence) and then breaks its own intervening trough (failure swing) signals trend exhaustion even while price still rises; the RSI double top above 70 / double bottom below 30 is the trigger.
setup_summary: RSI(9 or 14): >70 overbought, <30 oversold, 50 acts as trend midpoint (support during uptrend corrections, resistance to downtrend bounces). Sell setup: price at new high while RSI forms a double top above 70 (or descending RSI peaks), then RSI breaks the trough between its two peaks — a failure swing gives a sell signal even though price is still rising; often coincides with RSI falling back below 70. Buy setup is the mirror below 30. Most potent buy: daily AND weekly RSI both turning up from below 30.
trigger_invalidation: In strong trends RSI can stay above 70 for weeks — do not fade while pinned; divergence without the failure-swing confirmation is only a warning, not a signal. If weekly RSI is dropping while daily turns up, the daily buy signal is weak.
risk_geometry: Entry on bar close after the failure-swing confirmation; no explicit stop or target stated; 70/30 and 50 crossings themselves generate trend signals.
quote: If the RSI line then drops below the trough, a failure swing has been given.
chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'Welles Wilder's Relative Strength Index' / 'RSI Divergences' (pp.100-109)
notes: Distinct from stochastic finding: single-line divergence/failure-swing mechanics vs two-line cross with timeframe filter. RSI is computable on 1h data and widely corroborated. The failure-swing trigger is the falsifiable, objectively definable part.

strategy_name: Relative Strength Ratio Rotation (Top-Down Leadership)
mechanism: Money rotates among competing assets; the relative-strength ratio (asset/benchmark) trend reversal identifies which side is taking leadership, so investors buy rising-RS assets and avoid/underweight falling-RS assets.
setup_summary: Compute the RS ratio = asset price / benchmark (stock vs S&P 500; sector vs market; commodity vs bond; for crypto: coin vs BTC or an index). Apply trendline or moving-average analysis to the ratio: a break of a long down trendline in the ratio (e.g., CRB/S&P in 2002) signals new leadership; a downside violation of the ratio's 50-day MA (China/world ratio, Q4 2007) signals underperformance. Top-down process: establish market trend first, then the strongest sector/asset, then the leader within it — but require both relative strength AND an absolute uptrend (relative strength in a falling asset only means losing money more slowly).
trigger_invalidation: Ratio trendline/MA violation flips the rotation; diversification benefits diminish in global bear markets (all fall together).
risk_geometry: Entry only when the asset is in an absolute uptrend and its RS ratio is rising; no explicit stop/target or expiry stated.
quote: the relative strength ratio is the single most valuable tool in the asset allocation process
chapter_anchor: Ch.7 'The Relative Strength Ratio' (p.142) and Ch.9 'Relative Strength and Rotation' (pp.185-203)
notes: For V8, a coin/BTC (or altcoin/market-cap) RS ratio is a cross_market feature usable for selection and regime work; supported by extensive multi-year case studies but no formal statistics in this book. Crypto caveat: 2022-style regime shifts and stablecoin/benchmark composition changes need a frozen benchmark definition.

strategy_name: Relative strength ratio rotation (buy leaders, avoid laggards)
mechanism: relative strength ratio trend identifies leadership; concentration in leaders and rotation out of laggards captures the rotational drift that indexes hide
setup_summary: Compute the instrument/benchmark ratio (e.g., a sector or alt contract divided by the broad market). LONG the market or instrument whose RS ratio is above its rising trendline / making relative new highs while the benchmark is flat; exit and rotate when the RS ratio breaks its support trendline. Falsifiable: RS-ratio leaders persist over weeks-to-months and rotation into leaders on ratio-confirmation beats equal-weight.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: RS ratio above a rising trendline or breaking out vs benchmark. Invalidation: RS ratio closes through its support trendline (leadership loss) or the instrument's own trend turns.
risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close once ratio confirms. Stop: RS-ratio trendline break. Target/expiry: none stated; book notes sector trends may last only a few months so they must be monitored frequently.
quote: Relative strength analysis allows you to identify market sectors that are outperforming (leaders) and those that are underperforming (laggards). The main idea in doing that is to buy leading sectors and avoid the laggards.
chapter_anchor: Ch 12 Summary (Exchange-Traded Funds); also Ch 11 figs 11.6-11.7 (Consumer Staples RS high; Retail ratio support break)
notes: Direct analog in crypto perps: BTC/alt ratio and perp-vs-perp leader rotation (e.g., BTC vs ETH or sector contracts) as a cross_market feature. In 24/7 perp markets there are no exchange gaps to distort ratios, and funding regimes make the ratio the cleaner leadership gauge than absolute price. Requires the cross_market feature group and a benchmark series; single-instrument BTCUSDT 1h scope limits it to a candidate family.

strategy_name: 200-day moving average major-trend regime filter
mechanism: price below/above a very long MA defines the major trend; the MA's own slope adds regime confirmation
setup_summary: Track close relative to a long MA (book: 200-day). Close below the (rising) 200-day = major sell/risk-off; close above = major buy/risk-on; a turning-down 200-day is an additional bearish sign. Falsifiable: being flat or short while below the long MA and long while above it outperforms unconditional exposure.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close crosses the long MA. Invalidation: close returns through the MA (whipsaw) or the MA flattens into a range so the filter stops separating regimes.
risk_geometry: Used as a bias/regime gate, not an entry: no entry order, stop or R-target stated. In V8 terms it is a candidate RegimeFilter input that gates experts rather than a standalone expert.
quote: The fund fell below that major support line during July which flashed a major sell signal. ... It's a bad sign when the 200-day line turns down as it did near the end of that year.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11, '200-Day Moving Average and Housing' (fig 11.1); Ch 11 fig 11.10 (Fidelity Intl Real Estate); Ch 12 fig 12.2 (QQQQ)
notes: On V8's 1h bars a 200-day MA is ~4,800 bars; book uses daily. strategy_name: 50/200-day moving average crossover trend flip
mechanism: a shorter MA crossing a longer MA signals the intermediate trend has flipped; the cross filters noise that single-MA price violations cannot
setup_summary: Bullish cross: 50-period MA crosses above 200-period MA -> long bias; bearish cross: 50-period crosses below 200-period -> short bias. Book documents the bearish 50/200 cross as the second-stage sell signal (after the 200-day violation) that avoided two-thirds of a 30% drawdown. Falsifiable on BTCUSDT: cross-defined bias flips capture the major trend turns better than single-MA violations.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 50 MA crosses 200 MA. Invalidation: immediate counter-cross (whipsaw) or price stalling in a range where MAs converge.
risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close after cross confirmation. Exit: opposite cross. No R-multiples or stops stated; book treats it as a position bias tool.
quote: The second is the downside crossing of the 200-day average by the 50-day (down arrow) a month later. From its summer 2007 top to its spring 2008 bottom, this fund lost 30 percent of its value. The visual trader who spotted the bearish moving average crossing could have avoided two-thirds of those losses.

The 50/200 on 1h (~1,200/4,800 bars) is slow but maps directly to the trend feature group. Keep as a backlog family; low priority versus faster trend features, and it is effectively a variant of the long-MA regime filter.

strategy_name: Old resistance becomes new support (breakout retest hold)
mechanism: after an upside breakout of prior resistance, the first pullback to the breakout level acts as support; a hold-and-resume confirms genuine demand at the level
setup_summary: Price closes above a prior windowed high (breakout), then pulls back to the old-resistance/new-support level; if the close holds above the breakout level and price resumes the uptrend, continue LONG. Falsifiable: retest-holds above the breakout level are followed by continuation more often than retests that close back below.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: breakout close above prior high; retest close stays above breakout level. Invalidation: retest closes back below the breakout level (failed retest / vacuum reentry).
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close above resistance, or the retest-hold close. Stop: below the breakout level (retest low). Target: not stated (continuation, book gives no R-multiple).
quote: the fund dipped right back to its breakout point during August (see circle) before resuming its uptrend. That confirmed the old adage that 'old resistance becomes new support.'

Perp 24/7 markets have no gap-throughs of resistance levels, so breakout-level retests are cleaner and more testable; high leverage makes the stop below the breakout level a natural 1R geometry.

strategy_name: Rate-of-change zero-line crossing as trend confirmation
mechanism: ROC crossing zero after a long stretch on one side signals the trend has lost or regained momentum
setup_summary: Compute ROC(N) (book: 13-week ROC on weekly). A zero crossing after the ROC has been on the opposite side for an extended period (e.g., first time below zero in 16 months) confirms the trend change and is the tradeable signal. Falsifiable: ROC zero-crosses, especially after a long one-sided stretch, precede trend continuation in the cross direction.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: ROC(N) crosses zero after >=N bars one-sided. Invalidation: ROC re-crosses zero within a few bars (failure) or the move is range-bound.
risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close after zero-cross. No stop/target stated; used as a confirmation feature rather than a standalone system.
quote: A sell signal occurred in December 2007 (down arrow) when the rate of change fell below zero for the first time in 16 months.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11, 'Negative ROC Hurts Technology' (fig 11.5); ROC also indexed under 'Rate of change' usage in Ch 11 and Appendix A scans
notes: The 'first time in N months' qualification is the falsifiable part: a prior-context ROC zero-cross is stronger than a raw one. On 1h perp data, ROC over ~equivalent windows is cheap and deterministic. Add as a trend/response feature; the 'extended one-sided stretch' condition makes it a candidate regime-confirmation input, not an expert.

strategy_name: Point-and-figure column breakout with box-size sensitivity scaling
mechanism: recording only box-size price moves strips intra-column noise; a new column exceeding prior column tops/bottoms is an unambiguous breakout, and exceeding more columns is a stronger signal
setup_summary: Build a point-and-figure chart with a percent box size (book recommends 1% default; 0.5% for short-term, 2% for long-term). Buy signal: new X column exceeds the prior column's top (double-top breakout; triple/quadruple for exceeding 2-3 columns). Sell signal: new O column falls below prior bottoms. Falsifiable: the box-size-filtered column breakouts have higher follow-through than raw tick-by-tick breakouts, and triple/quadruple signals outrank double.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: column exceedance of prior column extreme. Invalidation: immediate column reversal (X->O or O->X) right after the signal.
risk_geometry: Entry: at the column-break signal price. Stop: at the box level where the column reverses (box size sets stop granularity). Target: not stated in Part 2; book notes P&F software computes price objectives.
quote: the triple-top breakout is considered to be a stronger signal. The same is true of the triple-bottom breakdown. And, as you might expect, the quadruple-top breakout is even stronger because three previous X columns are exceeded.
chapter_anchor: Appendix C, 'Triple and Quadruple Signals' (figs C.1-C.3, C.6); box-size guidance in 'How to Vary P&F Charts'

strategy_name: Multiple Time Frame Momentum Strategy (dual-timeframe momentum alignment)
mechanism: larger-timeframe momentum direction conditions the market; a smaller-timeframe momentum reversal in that direction is the highest-probability re-entry point
setup_summary: Trade only in the direction of the higher-timeframe momentum (e.g., 4h/1d trend feature); wait for a lower-timeframe (1h) momentum oscillator bullish/bearish reversal; enter with a stop-based trigger and initial stop one tick beyond the swing made prior to the reversal. Falsifiable: count entries that occur within N bars of a higher-TF bullish/bearish momentum state and a lower-TF cross.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = lower-TF momentum reversal in direction of higher-TF momentum, cancelled if the lower-TF momentum makes an opposite reversal before fill. Thesis invalid if the higher-TF momentum reverses or reaches OB/OS (see regime_filter finding); the book states a higher-TF bearish reversal from OB implies weeks of sideways-to-down, not a long.
risk_geometry: Entry via stop one tick above/below the last completed bar or swing; initial protective stop one tick below/above the swing prior to the reversal; ST unit target = minor corrective retracement, LT unit target = trend continuation.
quote: The basic strategy is to trade in the direction of the larger time frame and execute the trade following a smaller time frame momentum reversal in the direction of the larger time frame momentum.
chapter_anchor: Glossary 'Multiple Time Frame Momentum Strategy'; Ch.2 rules; Ch.7-8 trade campaigns
notes: The book calls this 'the best trade filter I've discovered in over 20 years'. V8's trend_pullback already encodes single-timeframe trend alignment; a dual-timeframe (4h/1d trend, 1h momentum reversal) variant is the natural refinement. Momentum = ROC-style oscillator, computable PIT. Requires a trend feature evaluated on a second timeframe bucket.

strategy_name: Momentum reversal trailing one-bar-high/low (Tr-1BH/L) stop entry
mechanism: entry only fills when price takes out the prior bar extreme in the trade direction, avoiding catching a knife and confirming momentum continuation
setup_summary: After the lower-timeframe momentum reversal condition is met, rest a stop order one tick above (long) or below (short) the last completed bar; re-arm the order on each new bar at the new bar extreme until filled; initial stop one tick beyond the swing low/high prior to entry. Falsifiable: entry fills only if the bar extreme is taken out; measurable fill rate and subsequent outcome.
trigger_invalidation: Order is cancelled if the smaller-timeframe momentum makes a reversal in the opposite direction before the fill; thesis invalid if the swing used for the initial stop is breached at fill time.
risk_geometry: Stop-entry at prior-bar extreme +1 tick; initial protective stop at swing low/high -1 tick; exposure = entry-to-stop distance (the book repeatedly computes initial capital exposure in pips and judges setups by it).
quote: If the trade entry order is executed, the initial protective stop is placed one tick below/above the swing low/high made prior to entry.

strategy_name: Swing breakout entry strategy
mechanism: a defined reversal/continuation condition plus price taking out a recent swing extreme confirms the new section has begun
setup_summary: Once minimum setup conditions are met (higher-TF momentum alignment, correction position), enter go-long one tick above the recent swing high (or go-short one tick below the recent swing low); initial stop one tick beyond the swing made prior to entry. Falsifiable: define swing via windowed pivot rule; entry triggers on breakout bar.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid if setup conditions (momentum/pattern position) are no longer true before price reaches the swing level, or if price reverses below/above the prior swing after entry.
risk_geometry: Stop-entry above/below recent swing extreme; initial stop at the prior swing +1 tick buffer; no target stated by this strategy (targets come from price projection methods).

strategy_name: Two-unit / multiple-unit exit management
mechanism: splitting one thesis into a short-term and long-term unit lets the trader bank a profit on a minor corrective target while keeping a wide-stop unit alive for the larger trend
setup_summary: Every trade taken with at least two units. Unit 1 (ST) is exited at a minor corrective target (e.g., the 50% retracement) or trailed at the one-bar-low after a lower-TF momentum reversal; Unit 2 (LT) is held for a trend target with a wide stop adjusted only on swing structure. Falsifiable: compare (a) two-unit exit scheme vs (b) all-in/all-out on the same entries.
trigger_invalidation: ST-unit exit triggers on minor-target touch or trailing 1BL; LT-unit exit triggers on trend target, higher-TF momentum extreme reversal, or swing-based stop; thesis invalid when the correction extends past its price/time targets (implies complex correction or reversal).
risk_geometry: ST unit: exit ~50% retracement or trailing 1BL after momentum reversal, then stop moved to breakeven; LT unit: stop kept far, adjusted one tick below/above swing prior to each momentum reversal; capital exposure measured per unit.
quote: Every trade should be taken with at least two units. One unit is considered short-term and is exited if the market reaches a minor corrective target. The second unit is considered long-term and is exited at a trend target.
chapter_anchor: Ch.7 / Glossary 'multiple-unit trading'; executed by Adam Sowinski (p.202-206), Jagir Singh (p.207-213), Jaime Johnson (p.231-235)
notes: Partial exits are compatible with V8's one-active-exposure rule (rule 16) since they scale one exposure rather than opening a second. The book also contains a scale-IN example (add to short below a minor Wave-b low); that conflicts with the one-exposure rule and would need explicit lifecycle treatment if ever pursued.

strategy_name: Wide-stop structure-based stop trailing (momentum-reversal stop adjustments)
mechanism: keeping the stop far from price early protects the trade from noise; tightening only on a technical event (momentum reversal, target touch) avoids being shaken out of a valid trend position
setup_summary: Initial stop one tick beyond the swing prior to entry; do not move it until a defined technical event occurs (target reached, or the next lower-TF momentum reversal). Then adjust to one tick beyond the swing low/high made prior to that reversal. Do not trail to every minor swing. Falsifiable: a rule 'adjust stop only on momentum-reversal events' versus 'trail at every N-bar swing' compared on outcome and stop-out rate.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger for each adjustment = momentum reversal event in trade direction (or structure change: consolidation breakout, gap, two-day selloff); thesis invalid if price exceeds the swing levels that define the stop chain (dead thesis).
risk_geometry: Stops at swing points +1 tick, not ATR multiples; the book's examples keep the LT stop so wide it only adjusts a handful of times over a multi-week trade (e.g., EUR/USD LT unit: stop moved ~3 times in 6 weeks).
quote: Unsuccessful traders often trail the stop much too close to the market and get stopped out for a relatively small profit when they could have held for a much larger profit.
chapter_anchor: Ch.8 Robert's Follow-Up on Adam Sowinski (p.205); also Ch.7 LT-unit management (p.193-196)
notes: Directly informs V8's dead-thesis (still_valid) vs stop distinction and the RiskGate stop model: the rule is that stops are adjusted on structure/momentum events, not continuously. In high-leverage perps this must be paired with the exposure cap (risk_percent_sizing finding) since wide stops mean large absolute risk.

strategy_name: Momentum OB/OS dual-timeframe regime filter (exhaustion block)
mechanism: when higher-timeframe momentum is overbought/oversold, the remaining move is limited and a higher-timeframe reversal is imminent, so new entries are blocked and existing stops tightened
setup_summary: Only long trades considered when higher-TF momentum is bullish UNLESS it is bull OB; only shorts when bearish UNLESS bear OS. When the higher-TF momentum reaches OB, expect at most a couple of lower-TF reversals before a higher-TF high/reversal; after a higher-TF bearish reversal from OB, expect sideways-to-down for several weeks (no new longs). Falsifiable: measure forward returns after higher-TF momentum extreme vs non-extreme, and after higher-TF reversal-from-extreme.
trigger_invalidation: Filter blocks new entries (RiskGate admission) at OB/OS extremes; once a higher-TF reversal from extreme occurs, the thesis 'trend continues' is invalid and existing positions are trailed tightly.
risk_geometry: No entry at extremes; existing LT positions trailed close (one tick below swing prior to next lower-TF reversal) once the dual-timeframe extreme position is made; anticipated high within a couple of higher-TF bars.
quote: Only long trades would be considered if the momentum is bullish unless the momentum is bull OB. ... The weekly momentum made a bearish reversal from the OB zone, which is typically followed by a sideways to down trend for several weeks, which is not a time to hold a long position.
chapter_anchor: Glossary 'bull OB, momentum'; Ch.2 strategy rules (referenced); Ch.7 p.196-197
notes: Crypto momentum extremes can persist (OB stays OB during sharp trend legs), so the 'imminent reversal' claim is the falsifiable part to test on BTCUSDT 1h with 4h/1d higher-TF momentum. As a RiskGate admission block it is cheap and testable.
book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

strategy_name: ABC-correction confluence-zone pullback entry (multi-Fib target cluster)
mechanism: corrections are at least three swings; their end is bracketed by a confluence of independent price projections (internal retracements, APP, external retracements) and time retracement, so the pullback low is a location feature rather than a guess
setup_summary: In an established trend, after a three-swing (ABC) correction, enter in trend direction when price reaches a zone where multiple Fib levels cluster (e.g., 61.8/78.6% internal retracements, 100% APP of Wave-A, 127/162% external retracements) with lower-TF momentum oversold (for a long) and time retracement in the 38.2-61.8% band. Falsifiable: define the confluence zone by counting overlapping projection levels; test touch-and-reversal frequency.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid if price breaks beyond the confluence zone toward the Wave-A extreme (simple ABC) or past 162% Ex-Ret / 100% time retracement (complex correction or trend reversal). A confirmed three-wave decline that reverses above the Wave-A low implies the correction is over and the advance continues (used as an exit in the GBP example).
risk_geometry: Entry via momentum-reversal/1BH trigger after the zone touch; initial stop below the confluence/support (e.g., below regression channel line); ST target = Wave-C target zone (61.8-100% APP); LT target = continuation beyond the prior extreme.
quote: Most corrections end at or very near one of the four key internal retracements.
chapter_anchor: Glossary 'retracement, internal price'; Ch.4 (referenced); Ch.8 Derrik Hobbs soybean setup (p.223-224)
notes: Refines trend_pullback: adds a location feature (confluence zone of windowed-Fib levels) as the expected pullback terminus, plus the time-retracement band. The three-swing assumption ('the assumption is always that a correction will make at least three sections') is the falsifiable core.
book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

strategy_name: 2-standard-deviation linear regression channel reversion/continuation
mechanism: in a trend, price oscillating around a 2-sd regression channel mean reverts at the channel edges, so the bottom of the channel locates the trend-continuation entry and the top locates the exit
setup_summary: In an established uptrend with weekly/daily momentum oversold, buy when price reaches the bottom of the 2-sd linear regression channel and a momentum bullish reversal fires; initial stop below the channel support; exit half at the channel median, the rest at the top of the channel. Falsifiable: measure reversion at the channel band and the median/top objective hit rate.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid if price closes below the regression channel support line (stop at a structural low under the line); a 'at least two-day sell-off before considering a swing low' rule governs which structure points count for stop adjustment.
risk_geometry: Entry at momentum reversal near channel bottom (767'25, stop 743'75 in the example); stop below regression support; exit half at channel median, half at channel top; the author admits this yields small losses in choppy, non-trending conditions and large gains in runaway trends.
quote: My objective in a strong trending market is to take half the profits at the median of the regression channel and to take the rest of the profits at the top of the regression channel.
chapter_anchor: Ch.8 Derrik Hobbs soybean trade (p.225-227)
notes: A 2-sd regression channel is the linear analogue of Bollinger bands; computable deterministically on bar closes. Crypto trends routinely overshoot channel edges during funding-driven squeezes, so the reversion assumption is the falsifiable part. Candidate backlog family; requires volatility (std-dev window), trend, and location features.

strategy_name: Dual Time Frame Momentum Strategy (direction + execution filter)
mechanism: When rate-of-change momentum on a larger time frame defines trade direction and a smaller time frame momentum reversal aligns with it, the market is positioned for the largest price moves with minimal capital exposure; momentum and price trends often diverge, so a single-frame momentum signal is not a trade signal.
setup_summary: On any two time frames (e.g., daily+60m, or 4h+1h for crypto), only consider trades in the direction of the larger time frame momentum indicator trend. The setup condition is a smaller time frame momentum reversal (fast line crossing slow line) in the direction of the larger time frame. Four higher-timeframe states with distinct rules: bull-not-OB (longs on smaller-TF bullish reversal below OB zone), bull-OB (no new longs, shorts possible on bearish reversal), bear-not-OS (shorts on smaller-TF bearish reversal above OS zone), bear-OS (no new shorts, longs possible on bullish reversal). Setup is a precondition, not an execution signal.
trigger_invalidation: Setup voided if smaller time frame momentum reverses against the larger time frame before execution; smaller-TF bullish reversal made inside the OB zone (or bearish reversal in the OS zone) is not a valid long (short) setup. A higher time frame OB/OS position is never a reason to exit an existing position, only to avoid new entries.
risk_geometry: Filter only: no entry/stop of its own; entry is handled by a separate objective entry strategy (e.g., trailing one-bar or swing). Higher-TF oversold/overbought lowers expected downside before the next reversal, reducing required capital exposure.
quote: Trade in the direction of the larger time frame momentum. Execute the trade following the smaller time frame momentum reversals.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, Multiple Time Frame Momentum Strategy (esp. 'The Basic Dual Time Frame Momentum Strategy' and 'Dual Time Frame Momentum Strategy Rules', Table 2.1)
notes: The author's core claim ('most powerful approach I've discovered in over 20 years'), fully objective (four momentum states, no interpretation). Book shows honest losing setups and divergences. In V8 terms this is a universal direction gate; because routers/shared scorers are ABSENT by default (rule 14), it must enter either as a per-expert feature requirement (e.g., trend_pullback already requires trend+volatility) or through a registry experiment beating a simpler baseline on frozen OOS. Crypto note: 24/7 tape makes two-frame momentum alignment well-defined with no session/gap artifacts, and the book's own 'momentum hangs in OB during strong trends' rule anticipates crypto's strong-trend behaviour.

strategy_name: ABC correction overlap + Wave-B-takeout continuation entry
mechanism: When a pullback section overlaps back into the range of the prior section, the market is most likely in a correction (not a new trend); a move beyond the Wave-B extreme confirms the correction is complete and price resumes the pre-correction trend to a new extreme.
setup_summary: In an established trend, label a pullback as at least three swings (A-B-C). Setup signal: price trades back into the range of Wave-A (the overlap guideline) - minimum conditions for a correction are complete. Entry: trade/close beyond the Wave-B extreme (a swing entry) - 'all-out go long or short signal' - with the initial protective stop no further than the potential Wave-C extreme. Minimum expectation: a new extreme beyond where the correction began. On the opposite side, a trend is the five-wave non-overlapping structure.
trigger_invalidation: If price takes out the extreme that began the prior trend (the correction thesis level), the correction interpretation is voided. Book is explicit that overlap is not always a correction and a correction is not always overlapping (two shown failure figures), so stop discipline at the Wave-C extreme is mandatory.
risk_geometry: Entry: 1 tick beyond Wave-B extreme (swing takeout). Initial stop: 1 tick beyond potential Wave-C extreme (the swing low/high prior to entry). No fixed target: minimum reward is the new extreme beyond the correction start; 100% alternate price projection is the usual reward assumption. No fixed expiry.
quote: If a market overlaps a section, more than likely it is making a correction. ... A trade beyond the Wave-B extreme is a pattern signal that the correction should be complete, with a stop no further than the potential Wave-C extreme.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Trend or Correction: The Overlap Guideline' and 'ABC and Away We Go'
notes: Structure-based and timeframe-agnostic, so it transfers to 1h/4h crypto, but requires reliable swing labeling (the book's own failed-example Figure 3.17 shows a 'correction' that broke down to new lows) and the author admits 'most corrections do have a swing overlap and most overlaps are a part of a correction' without statistics. New family means a registry decision + CHANGELOG per D-032/D-033; complexity budget (rule 14) is full at 3 active experts, so this must start in backlog (like breakout_retest and capitulation).

strategy_name: Five-wave trend stage identification ('fifth waves are the key')
mechanism: Trends typically complete in five non-overlapping sections; once four sections conforming to guidelines are confirmed, the next new extreme is probably a final Wave-5 and the trend is near exhaustion, so the countermove should be at least greater in time and price than any correction within the trend.
setup_summary: Count trend sections; when four completed sections meet the guidelines (Wave-2 does not trade beyond the start of Wave-1; Wave-3 is not the shortest of waves 1, 3, 5; Wave-4 does not close into the closing range of Wave-1 - author's modification allows intraday wick overlap), a new extreme is a probable Wave-5. A smaller time frame momentum reversal at the probable Wave-5 extreme is an early signal the trend is complete. A trade beyond the Wave-4 extreme confirms five waves done and implies a countermove at least greater in time and price than any prior correction in the trend.
trigger_invalidation: Count invalidated (recount) if Wave-2 exceeds the Wave-1 origin, Wave-3 is the shortest, or Wave-4 closes into the Wave-1 closing range. The book shows overlapping bull 'trend' waves (Figure 3.28) where the structure never conformed - so this is a heuristic stage cue, not a rule.
risk_geometry: Exit/stage rule rather than entry: when the four-wave guidelines are met and momentum reverses at a probable Wave-5, tighten or trail stops instead of adding; reversal entry only after Wave-4 extreme takeout with a stop beyond the Wave-5 extreme.
quote: The most valuable piece of information regarding trends is that once waves 1 through 4 are confirmed, the trend should be in the final stages.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Trends and Five-Wave Patterns' and 'Fifth Waves Are the Key'
notes: For V8 this is best used as a lifecycle/exit-side rule for existing trend experts (a 'trend near exhaustion' state that flips the still_valid or stop-trailing policy) rather than a standalone entry, consistent with the book using it to avoid adding longs near the end of a trend. In 24/7 high-leverage perps, extended fifth waves and liquidation cascades are common, and the author's own modification (allow wick overlap of Wave-1) plus the overlapping-trend example argue for keeping it a probabilistic stage cue.

strategy_name: Dynamic Price Strategy: In-Ret + APP + Ex-Ret confluence zones (EOW targets)
mechanism: Corrective and trend highs/lows tend to occur at proportions of prior sections; a narrow price zone where independent projections from different sets (internal retracements, alternate price projections, external retracements) coincide marks a high-probability reversal zone for a correction or trend end.
setup_summary: Internal retracements: 38.2/50/61.8/78.6% of a trend section (50/61.8 end most corrections; 78.6 is the max - a close beyond it voids the correction thesis). Alternate price projections: for a correction, APP of Wave-A at 61.8/100/162 projected from the B extreme (100% APP is the most frequent target); for a five-wave trend with four sections complete, APP of waves 1-3 at 38.2/61.8 from the Wave-4 extreme and 100% APP of Wave-1. External retracements: 127/162/262% of Wave-B (correction) or Wave-4 (trend) to locate the final section. A high-probability zone contains one projection from each of the three sets (minimum: one In-Ret plus one APP).
trigger_invalidation: If price reaches the zone without a momentum/pattern reversal, the zone is not the end of the structure. A close through the 78.6% internal retracement voids the correction thesis (trend continuing). Corrective sections rarely exceed the 162% APP.
risk_geometry: These are pre-identified take-profit/reversal zones, not entries - the book insists entries still require confirmation (never buy/sell at a target price). Reward estimation rule: the minimum reward is a new extreme beyond where the correction began, or the 100% APP; 'risk/reward' ratios are called a best guess and deprecated.
quote: if an In-Ret and an APP are near each other, they form a relatively narrow-range zone from where a corrective trend reversal is probable.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, 'Beyond Fib Retracements' (Internal Retracements, Alternate Price Projections, External Retracements, Pattern Price Targets / EOW-C and EOW-5)
notes: Ratios are price-agnostic and computable on 1h bars, but in leveraged 24/7 perps projected zones are frequently swept by stop-runs and liquidation cascades, so the book's own prescription - zone reached is only a condition to stand ready for a momentum/pattern reversal, never a standalone trade - is the load-bearing part. For V8 these zones are natural 'location' feature-group inputs (distance-to-confluence-zone features) rather than a new expert, and could later feed take-profit placement as a refinement of the fixed target_r 1.0 convention.

strategy_name: Two-unit position: short-term take at minor-correction completion, long-term unit rides the trend
mechanism: Splitting a position into two units hedges the uncertainty of the larger trend call: exiting the first unit at a probable minor-correction completion banks a profit even when the 'major trend' thesis is wrong, while the second unit is held with a wide stop to capture a developing trend.
setup_summary: Every position is taken in at least two units. Short-term unit: once price reaches the 61.8% retracement of the prior trend section OR after the second smaller time frame momentum reversal against the position (two reversals because even a corrective rally makes an ABC with two momentum highs), trail the stop at the 1-bar low and take the unit out on the trailing stop. Long-term unit: hold with a relatively wide stop (e.g., below the potential Wave-B low / out of the typical 38.2-50% Wave-4 retracement) until the higher time frame momentum reaches its overbought/oversold extreme or a probable Wave-C / Wave-5 price target is reached, then trail the 1-bar low; adjust to breakeven once two sections of a potential ABC are complete.
trigger_invalidation: ST unit exits on the trailing 1-bar low after its trigger (61.8% retracement or second momentum reversal). LT unit exits on the trailing 1-bar low after higher-TF momentum OB/OS or the projected Wave-C/Wave-5 target zone; the book's example also shows a logical mid-campaign stop advance after a minor swing high was taken out.
risk_geometry: Two exits per position: unit-1 target is a structural retracement/momentum condition, unit-2 target is trend-exhaustion (higher-TF momentum extreme or pattern/price target), both executed as trailing 1-bar-low stops rather than fixed-price limits. Aggregate capital exposure still capped at 3% (see risk_percent_sizing).
quote: For every trade, there must be at least two units. ... one unit is usually exited relatively quickly for a relatively small profit. The second unit is held with the intention of capturing the longer-term trend.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, 'Multiple-Unit Trading' and 'Trade Management' (XAU and S&P campaigns)
notes: Partial takes fit perp trading well: they harvest the fast initial move, cap losses when the 'trend' call is wrong, and cut exposure (and funding cost) on the second unit. In V8, rule 16 allows one exposure per (instrument, direction) - a two-unit position is a within-exposure sizing variant, not two exposures, so this is a lifecycle refinement requiring a registry decision, not a new expert family.

strategy_name: Let-the-market-take-you-out: trailing stop, never exit at a fixed price target
mechanism: Fixed take-profit exits forfeit the tail of trends (markets often blow through price targets); trailing a protective stop keyed to structure and momentum captures the majority of a trend while capping the give-back, because the stop is always placed at the price that voids the trade thesis.
setup_summary: After entry, never place a take-profit at a predetermined price; instead trail the protective stop at the trailing 1-bar low or below the most recent minor swing structure, advancing it only on a logical structural event: a new minor swing extreme taken out, the second smaller-TF momentum reversal against the position, price reaching a 61.8% retracement or a projected target zone (as a stop-adjustment trigger, not an exit price), or the higher time frame momentum reaching OB/OS. Exit is the stop being hit by market action. Exception allowed: when you cannot monitor the market (e.g., vacation), leave a protective stop plus a take-profit limit.
trigger_invalidation: The stop is never placed at an arbitrary dollar distance from price; it is always at the price that voids the entry thesis. The four exit concepts: (1) let the market take you out, (2) exit factors = entry factors (momentum/pattern/price/time), (3) plan both units' exits before entry, (4) adjust as new information arrives, each change a logical consequence of the new bars.
risk_geometry: Stop = 1 tick beyond trailing 1-bar low or the relevant swing structure; no fixed target; expiry = while the thesis holds, exits are structural. Gives back a small amount beyond each swing to avoid premature exits ('trailing a stop too close' is named the top reason traders get shaken out before trend completion).
quote: Always let the market take you out by moving against the position. Do not exit at a predetermined price target.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, 'Exit Strategies' and 'Exit Strategy Concepts'
notes: Directly applicable to perps, where early-profit-taking is the dominant retail habit and trends are extended; one caveat the book does not address: funding costs on a held long mean an 'always hold to trend end' bias must be tempered by expected funding carry. For V8 this argues for making still_valid/dead-thesis exits structural (already the design: stops and dead-thesis are different exits) and for refining target_r handling so projected zones are stop-tightening triggers rather than hard take-profits.

strategy_name: Momentum lookback selection: variants, not one magic setting
mechanism: An indicator's lookback period sets the tradeoff between signal lag and whipsaw false reversals; the useful setting for a market/timeframe is the one where reversals originate from the OB/OS zones near price extremes with few mid-range fakes, and settings must be re-tuned when volatility/momentum cycles change.
setup_summary: For a chosen momentum indicator (Stoch/DTosc/MACD are shown to give nearly identical reversal timing - 'most price indicators represent about the same thing'), test a few lookback periods (e.g., 8 vs 13 vs 21) on recent data: the 13-period example beat 8 (mid-range whipsaws) and 21 (lag + reversals missing the OB/OS zones). Choose the period meeting three criteria: (1) both lines reach the OB/OS zone before most reversals, (2) reversals fall within a couple bars of price swing extremes, (3) few whipsaw reversals between zones. Re-test when momentum cycles change (e.g., when the indicator stops reaching the OS zone on corrections in a stronger trend, shorten the lookback).
trigger_invalidation: Settings drift: when the indicator makes two or more oscillations without reaching the OB/OS zones on corrections, the lookback is no longer matched to the current momentum cycle and should be revised on recent data.
risk_geometry: n/a (parameter selection); the author explicitly rejects the idea of one universal best setting and of market-condition-dependent rule sets (never know a trading range/trend in advance), arguing for one chosen setting held until compelling evidence of drift.
quote: Test a few settings on recent data and see which best meets the criteria for a useful indicator.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'What Are the Best Indicator Settings to Use?'
notes: This validates V8's rule that parameter/threshold changes are VARIANTS of one family (one multiplicity unit) rather than new experts, and warns that crypto's volatile regime changes will invalidate fixed lookbacks - re-tuning must be done on frozen OOS with a registry decision (per rule 15), never in-sample or on live data, to respect V8 determinism and the no-overfit gate.

strategy_name: Four-factor confluence: momentum + pattern + price + time alignment
mechanism: When several independent market dimensions (multiple time frame momentum, pattern structure, projected price zone, projected time window) all indicate the same reversal, the setup has a higher probability outcome and smaller capital exposure than any single factor alone, because the odds stack rather than add.
setup_summary: For each candidate reversal, score four independent factors: (1) multiple time frame momentum position and smaller-TF reversal, (2) pattern position (ABC completion / overlap / five-wave stage), (3) price projections confluence zone reached, (4) time projections window reached. Trade only when multiple factors point to the same reversal; the book's worked campaigns (XAU, S&P, OIH) always list Momentum/Pattern/Price/Time summaries before the Trade Strategy. Minimum expectation rule used throughout: after a completed correction/trend, price resumes to a new extreme at least greater in time and price than the prior section.
trigger_invalidation: When factors conflict, treat the setup as lower probability - pass or reduce size; never take a trade on a single factor. The book is explicit that any single indicator or technique alone is insufficient and that all four together still lose sometimes (objective is 'high probability outcome and acceptable capital exposure', never certainty).
risk_geometry: Confluence lowers initial capital exposure because the entry sits at the alignment point with a close structural stop (book example: ~2-3 points risk against 35+ points reward). The reward side is always a best guess (minimum = new extreme beyond correction start, or 100% APP).
quote: it is when several completely independent factors all indicate the same position that the best setups with the highest probability outcome and smallest capital exposure are made.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Momentum and Pattern Position'; thesis restated in Chapters 4-5 summaries and every Chapter 7 trade campaign
notes: The confluence thesis is coherent with V8's multi-feature-group experts (each setup already requires several feature groups), but the independent contribution of each factor in 24/7 leveraged crypto is unknown and must be validated per factor (e.g., feature-gate ablation on frozen OOS). This is a methodology lesson for how setups are composed in MarketState, not a new expert or a router - the absence-by-default rule (rule 14) means a shared confluence scorer would have to win a registry experiment.

strategy_name: Rejected: momentum-divergence reversal systems and 'trading range' strategies
mechanism: The author's falsification stance: price-momentum divergence and trading-range patterns are selected-after-the-fact artifacts; divergence occurs when a trend merely slows (momentum reverses while price continues), so most divergence-setup 'reversals' are losses, and a trading range can never be known to be a range in advance.
setup_summary: The author challenges any single-indicator or divergence-based system: 'I've never seen one of these plans that actually made money' despite many well-chosen published examples, because on the same data there were identical divergence setups that lost. Likewise, 'trading range strategies' are declared fiction since the market can never be known in advance to be entering a range - the book shows the same pattern position (overlap) failing to a new low. Explicit caution to ignore educators selling divergence or range-specific rules.
trigger_invalidation: n/a - rejection stance; the relevant test is that any divergence/range rule must survive PROJECT_EVIDENCE on frozen OOS before V8 ever formalizes it.
risk_geometry: n/a
quote: I've never seen one of these plans that actually made money... For every price-momentum divergence example that resulted in a trend reversal, I can just about guarantee there were one or two and probably a lot more that did not result in a trend reversal on the same data.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'Momentum and Price Trends Often Diverge'; trading-range remarks in Chapters 2-3
notes: This is the author's skeptical argument, not empirical evidence - hence NARRATIVE - but it is a valuable screening gate for V8: divergence-based reversals (rsi_divergence and similar) and range-regime rules should not be adopted from literature alone; they need PROJECT_EVIDENCE_SUPPORTED before any registry movement. It also corroborates V8's core stance that trend indicators alone are unreliable for reversal timing ('for every trend indicator example I will show you two where it quickly failed').

strategy_name: Directional-volatility measurement (close-SD vs average range/ATR)
mechanism: Standard deviation of closes captures directional (trending) volatility that average range/ATR misses; two streams with identical average ranges can have very different SD, so volatility filters and stop distances must be computed on a measure matched to the intended risk.
setup_summary: Given two 18-bar streams with identical high-low ranges each bar, one trending (closes drifting) and one ranging, average range is equal but SD of closes is far higher for the trending stream. The book's catastrophic stops are 3-SD of closing price (not ATR), and the author 'always checks both measures' when using a volatility filter; he also notes the 40-day SD of closes varies within a commodity by an order of magnitude (e.g., Nasdaq 100 from $1,140 to $46,500), which is why stops must be relative to recent volatility.
trigger_invalidation: Switching volatility measures changes stop-distance distributions; any change must be a frozen, audited feature-group decision and re-validated OOS.
risk_geometry: feeds stop placement: stops relative to recent volatility; book's canonical catastrophic stop = 3 SD of closing price.
quote: standard deviation accounts for directional volatility, while average range doesn't... I always check both measures when I use a volatility filter.
chapter_anchor: Appendix A 'Volatility Measures and Comparison', pp. 246-247; Appendix B 'Relative Contract Risk', pp. 252-255
notes: V8's atr_ref uses ATR (non-directional); this supports adding a close-SD-over-window volatility feature to audit whether directional-volatility regimes (trend segments) behave differently for stop placement. Adding a feature-group member is a frozen-spec, audited change per D-031/D-032.

strategy_name: Donchian channel breakout trend-following (20-bar)
mechanism: trend persistence after channel breakout; entry at channel extreme gives momentum continuation with long-side profit 2-3x short side
setup_summary: Go long when price exceeds the highest close of the previous 20 bars; short when price breaks below the lowest close of the previous 20 bars; entry on a stop order at the breakout level; reversal exit when the opposite extreme is broken. On BTCUSDT 1h this maps to a 20-bar channel close breakout with reversal exit.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close above prior 20-bar highest close (long) / below prior 20-bar lowest close (short). Thesis invalidates if the longer-term trend filter (close vs close ~200 bars ago) no longer agrees with the entry direction.
risk_geometry: Entry on stop order at channel extreme; 3x 20-day standard-deviation catastrophic stop (avg ~$1,910/contract) triggered on close with exit next open; reversal exit otherwise; no time stop (trends have no time constraint).

strategy_name: Path-of-least-resistance tendency analysis
mechanism: each market class and timeframe has a persistent tendency to trend or to mean-revert; trading the direction of least resistance dominates blindly assuming a strategy style
setup_summary: Three-step monthly test on the target instrument: (1) baseline buy-and-hold; (2) buy instruments one std-dev above their 20-bar average (trend-following side); (3) buy instruments one std-dev below (counter-trend side). The side that beats baseline is the path of least resistance. For BTCUSDT 1h this decides between trend-following and mean-reversion expert families before any strategy development.
trigger_invalidation: Not an entry; a pre-development regime diagnostic. Its output is only valid for the tested timeframe - the book found stocks counter-trend on daily bars but trend on hourly bars, so a 1h result does not transfer to 4h/1d.
risk_geometry: No trade geometry; output is a per-timeframe tendency classification used to seed the entry-family choice.
quote: I believe stocks are primarily counter-trend-following tendency instruments on daily data; commodities are primarily trend-following instruments on daily data; and overall, FX pairs are primarily counter-trend-following tendency instruments.

strategy_name: One-day pullback entry filter on an existing trend setup
mechanism: most trend signals fire on up-close bars; waiting one adverse close after confirmation yields a better price and prunes entries at the top of the move that would go straight to the stop
setup_summary: If the long setup exists, wait for a down close; if the setup still exists, enter long on the next open. For shorts, wait for an up close. On BTCUSDT 1h: a valid long signal (e.g., Donchian breakout with trend filter) followed by one down bar, then entry at the next bar open.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: setup exists AND today's close is down (long) / up (short). Invalidation: the base setup no longer satisfies its conditions after the adverse close, or the longer-term trend filter flips.
risk_geometry: Entry next-open after the adverse close; no additional stop specified - inherits the base system's volatility stop; the standalone day-filter test (down-close day -> buy next open) made +$19/trade long, +$7/trade short across 56 commodities.
quote: If the long setup exists, we wait for price to go down one day, and if the setup still exists, we enter the long position. For shorts, we wait for price to rally for one day.

strategy_name: Longer-term trend alignment filter (close vs close N bars ago)
mechanism: only taking entries aligned with the longer-term trend direction removes counter-trend noise trades; a 70-bar lookback maximized gain-to-pain on both the stock and commodity systems
setup_summary: Gate every entry: long entries allowed only if today's close > close N bars ago (N=70 selected); short entries only if close < close N bars ago. On BTCUSDT 1h, a 70-bar regime gate. This filter alone kept the stock system out of most of the 2008 crash.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger condition is a monotonic close-vs-close comparison; invalidation is the trend comparison flipping against the open position's direction (dead-thesis exit source).
risk_geometry: No stop change; in the commodity system the 70-bar filter raised profit-per-trade 378->545, cut max drawdown 474k->355k, gain-to-pain 1.14->1.23.
quote: We only take trades if they are in the same direction as the longer-term trend, as determined by a comparison of today's close with that of x days ago.

strategy_name: Momentum divergence at channel extremes - fade, not trade
mechanism: in trending instruments, price/momentum divergence at a Donchian extreme is exhaustion, not continuation - trading divergences lost on stocks and commodities, while fading them on commodities won +$451/trade at 30 bars
setup_summary: 14-day Donchian high higher than the prior high, with a 14-bar momentum reading lower than at the prior high, and today's close below yesterday's (divergence short setup). Fade it: enter short on the next open instead of buying; hold 5-30 bars. Mirror for the long side at Donchian lows. On commodities the fade earned $136/trade at 5 bars rising to $451 at 30 bars.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence setup at a 14-bar channel extreme. Invalidation of the fade thesis: momentum moving back in the same direction as price (the book's alternative ruleset 'New price buy/sell setup' removed the opposite-momentum requirement and lost money).
risk_geometry: Market entry next open; fixed hold of 5-30 bars; no stops in the test - a crude exit that still won, so the entry is the load-bearing element.
quote: I think we can conclude that divergence trading doesn't have a significant edge in either stock or commodity trading; in fact, for commodities you'd be much better off trading in the opposite direction on each divergence signal.

strategy_name: Momentum divergence as trend-exhaustion warning
mechanism: price making a new extreme while momentum fails to confirm indicates the trend is decelerating/exhausting
setup_summary: On the trading timeframe, price prints a higher high while RSI(14) prints a lower high (bearish divergence) or price prints a lower low while RSI prints a higher low (bullish divergence). Divergence must be anchored on confirmed swing extremes (peak preceded and followed by opposite bars), allow ~2-3 bars tolerance between price and momentum peaks, and be invalidated if momentum re-pierces its prior extreme before price confirms.
trigger_invalidation: Divergence is null if the momentum indicator re-makes its prior peak/trough before the price peak/trough is confirmed; peaks offset by 4-5+ bars do not count; Kase: the setup becomes a usable exit/danger sign only when the divergence completes on a confirming closing bar.
risk_geometry: Book gives no entry/stop/target for this signal; used as a warning of trend change or (Kase) as an exit signal — pull stops to Dev2/Dev3 or warning line on divergence completion; OBOS levels are trend-conditional (uptrend: overbought 75-80 / oversold 35-40; downtrend: overbought 55-60 / oversold 20-25).
quote: Bearish divergence (an opportunity to sell) occurs when price is making higher highs and RSI is making lower highs.

strategy_name: KaseSwing higher-low swing-midpoint breakout
mechanism: after a higher swing low forms, a close above the intermediate swing high confirms the higher-low sequence and captures the next swing leg
setup_summary: Identify swing highs/lows with KaseSwing (swing size = N bars up/down, 1-3 typical; inside-bar and extreme rules defined). When the second swing low is >= the first swing low, go long on the bar that closes above the middle swing high between the two lows; mirror for shorts (second swing high <= first, close below middle swing low).
trigger_invalidation: Entry invalid if price breaks the prior swing low before the midpoint is reclaimed; open position exits when the trailing swing stop is broken.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close above the swing midpoint (fill-at-close compatible). Stop: prior swing low, ratcheted up at each new higher swing low; no target — exit on swing-stop break. Book caveat: swing stops are logical but not predictable in size, so cap the stop using the recent average of swing magnitudes or switch to DevStops.
quote: if there are two swing lows where the second swing low is equal to or higher than the first, then when prices exceed the middle swing high, a long trade may be taken
chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, 'Using KaseSwing for Market Timing' (pp. 163-168)
